title.zh: 卷二百六十六 列傳第二十五 錢若水 蘇易簡 郭贄 李至 辛仲甫 王沔 溫仲舒 王化基
title.en: Volume 266 Biographies 25: Qian Ruoshui, Su Yijian, Guo Zhi, Li Zhi, Xin Zhongfu, Wang Mian, Wen Zhongshu, Wang Huaji
title.raw: 卷二百六十六 列傳第二十五 錢若水 蘇易簡 郭贄 李至 辛仲甫 王沔 溫仲舒 王化基 Volume 266 Biographies 25: Qian Ruoshui, Su Yijian, Guo Zhi, Li Zhi, Xin Zhongfu, Wang Mian, Wen Zhongshu, Wang Huaji

sentences.zh: 錢若水

translations.literal: Qian Ruoshui
translations.idiomatic: Qian Ruoshui

sentences.zh: 錢若水，字澹成，一字長卿，河南新安人。

translations.literal: Qian Ruoshui, styled Dancheng, also styled Changqing, was a man of Xin'an in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Ruoshui, courtesy name Dancheng and also known as Changqing, was a native of Xin'an in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父文敏，漢青州帥劉銖辟為錄事參軍，歷長水酆都尉、扶風令、相州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His father Wen Min was summoned by Liu Zhu, commander of Qingzhou under Han, as Recording Secretary, and successively served as Commandant of Changshui and Feng, Magistrate of Fufeng, and Recording Secretary of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wen Min entered the service of Liu Zhu, military governor of Qingzhou under the Later Han, as recording secretary, and went on to hold the posts of commandant of Changshui and Feng, magistrate of Fufeng, and recording secretary of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，府帥多以筆牘私取官庫錢，韓重贇領節制，頗仍其弊。

translations.literal: Previously, prefectural commanders often took money from the official treasury privately by written order; Han Chongyun held military control and largely continued this abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, many prefectural commanders had privately drawn funds from the government treasury through written requisitions, and when Han Chongyun took command he largely continued the practice.

sentences.zh: 文敏不從，重贇假他事廷責之，文敏不為屈。

translations.literal: Wen Min would not comply; Chongyun used another matter to rebuke him in court, but Wen Min did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Min refused to go along, whereupon Chongyun seized on another matter to denounce him at court, yet Wen Min would not bend.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉其有守，授右讚善大夫、知瀘州，召見講武殿，謂曰：「瀘州近蠻境，尤宜綏撫。

translations.literal: Taizu praised his integrity, appointed him Right Supporter of Goodness Grandee and prefect of Luzhou, summoned him to an audience in the Hall of Martial Lectures, and said: 'Luzhou lies near the barbarian frontier and especially needs pacification and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu admired his steadfastness, made him Right Supporter of Goodness Grandee and prefect of Luzhou, and received him in audience at the Hall of Martial Lectures, saying, "Luzhou lies close to the barbarian borderlands and above all must be governed with conciliation.

sentences.zh: 聞知州郭思齊、監軍郭重遷掊斂不法，恃其荒遠，謂朝廷不知爾。

translations.literal: I have heard that the prefect Guo Siqi and the military inspector Guo Chongqian extort unlawfully, trusting in the remoteness of the region and thinking the court does not know.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the prefect Guo Siqi and the military inspector Guo Chongqian are extorting the people in violation of the law, trusting that their post is so remote the court will never find out.

sentences.zh: 至，為朕鞫之，苟一毫有侵於民，朕必不赦。」

translations.literal: When you arrive, investigate this for Us; if even a hair's breadth harms the people, We shall certainly not pardon them.'
translations.idiomatic: When you arrive, investigate them for me, and if they have harmed the people in the slightest degree, I shall show them no mercy."

sentences.zh: 至郡，有政跡，夷人詣闕借留。

translations.literal: When he reached the prefecture he achieved good administration, and the barbarians went to the capital to request that he be kept on.
translations.idiomatic: After he took up his post, his governance won praise, and the tribal peoples went to court to ask that he be retained.

sentences.zh: 詔改殿中丞，許再任。

translations.literal: An edict changed his rank to Palace Attendant and permitted him to serve another term.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attendant by imperial order and allowed to serve a second term.

sentences.zh: 三遷司封員外郎，又知洺州、建昌軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred three times to become an outer-office clerk in the Bureau of Enfeoffments, and also served as prefect of Mingzhou and Jianchang Military Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he reached the post of outer-office clerk in the Bureau of Enfeoffments, and later served as prefect of Mingzhou and of Jianchang Military Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 若水幼聰悟，十歲能屬文。

translations.literal: Ruoshui was clever and perceptive in youth; at ten he could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui was exceptionally bright as a child and could compose essays by the age of ten.

sentences.zh: 華山陳摶見之，謂曰：「子神清，可以學道；

translations.literal: Chen Tuan of Mount Hua saw him and said: 'Your spirit is clear; you may study the Way;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tuan of Mount Hua met him and said, "Your spirit is unusually clear; you could cultivate the Way;

sentences.zh: 不然，當富貴，但忌太速爾。」

translations.literal: if not, you will attain wealth and honor, but beware of attaining them too swiftly.'
translations.idiomatic: otherwise you are destined for wealth and high rank, though you must beware of rising too quickly."

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，舉進士，釋褐同州觀察推官，聽決明允，郡治賴之。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he passed the jinshi examination, took his first office as investigating censor under the Tongzhou observation commission, and his judgments were clear and fair, on which the prefecture's governance relied.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi period he passed the jinshi examination and took his first appointment as investigating censor under the Tongzhou observation commission; his decisions were lucid and equitable, and the prefecture came to depend on him.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，寇準掌選，薦若水洎王扶、程肅、陳充、錢熙五人文學高第，召試翰林，若水最優，擢秘書丞、直史館。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua, Kou Zhun controlled selection and recommended Ruoshui together with Wang Fu, Cheng Su, Chen Chong, and Qian Xi—five men of outstanding literary learning—for a trial examination at the Hanlin Academy; Ruoshui ranked highest and was promoted to secretary of the Secretariat and academician of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chunhua era Kou Zhun oversaw civil appointments and recommended Ruoshui, together with Wang Fu, Cheng Su, Chen Chong, and Qian Xi, as five scholars of exceptional literary attainment. Summoned to a trial examination at the Hanlin Academy, Ruoshui placed first and was appointed secretary of the Secretariat and academician of the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷右正言、知制誥。

translations.literal: After somewhat more than a year he was transferred to Right Remonstrator and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was made Right Remonstrator and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 會置理檢院於乾元門外，命若水領之。

translations.literal: When the Court of Petition Review was established outside the Qianyuan Gate, Ruoshui was ordered to head it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Court of Petition Review was set up outside the Qianyuan Gate, Ruoshui was placed in charge of it.

sentences.zh: 俄同知貢舉，加屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon he served concurrently as associate chief examiner of the civil service examinations and was given the additional title of outer-office clerk in the Bureau of State Farms.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he served as associate chief examiner and was given the additional rank of outer-office clerk in the Bureau of State Farms.

sentences.zh: 詔詣原、鹽等州制置邊事，還奏合旨，翌日，改職方員外郎、翰林學士，與張洎並命。

translations.literal: By edict he was sent to Yuan, Yan, and other prefectures to arrange frontier affairs; on his return his memorial accorded with the emperor's intent, and the next day he was changed to outer-office clerk in the Bureau of Military Appointments and Hanlin academician, appointed together with Zhang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to Yuan, Yan, and other prefectures to organize frontier affairs. When he returned, his memorial pleased the emperor, and the next day he was made outer-office clerk in the Bureau of Military Appointments and Hanlin academician, receiving the appointment together with Zhang Ji.

sentences.zh: 俄知審官院、銀臺通進封駁司。

translations.literal: Soon he also directed the Court of Official Review and the Silver Terrace Office for Transmission, Presentation, and Memorial Rebuttal.
translations.idiomatic: He soon also took charge of the Court of Official Review and the Silver Terrace Office for Transmission, Presentation, and Memorial Rebuttal.

sentences.zh: 嘗草賜趙保忠詔，有云：「不斬繼遷，開狡兔之三穴，潛疑光嗣，持首鼠之兩端。」

translations.literal: He once drafted an edict bestowed on Zhao Baozhong that read: 'If Jiqian is not beheaded, you open the three burrows of the crafty hare; if you secretly suspect Guangsi, you hold to both ends like a wavering rodent.'
translations.idiomatic: He once drafted an edict for Zhao Baozhong that declared, "If you do not destroy Jiqian, you leave the crafty hare his three burrows; if you secretly distrust Guangsi, you waver between two courses like a timid rodent."

sentences.zh: 太宗大以為當。

translations.literal: Taizong greatly approved of it as fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong thought the wording exactly right.

sentences.zh: 至道初，以右諫議大夫同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao he served as Right Remonstrance Grandee and associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhidao era he became Right Remonstrance Grandee and associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，加工部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded, he was given the additional title of Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong came to the throne, Ruoshui was given the additional rank of vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 數月，以母老上章，求解機務，詔不許。

translations.literal: After several months, citing his mother's age, he submitted a memorial requesting release from confidential state affairs; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later, pleading that his mother was elderly, he submitted a memorial asking to be relieved of confidential duties, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 若水請益堅，遂以本官充集賢院學士、判院事。

translations.literal: Ruoshui's request grew firmer, and he was then made, while retaining his original rank, academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and administrator of the institute.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruoshui pressed his request more insistently, he was allowed to keep his existing rank while serving as academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and administrator of the institute.

sentences.zh: 俄詔修《太宗實錄》，若水引柴成務、宗度、吳淑、楊億同修，成八十卷。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to compile the Veritable Records of Taizong; Ruoshui brought in Chai Chengwu, Zong Du, Wu Shu, and Yang Yi to compile together, completing eighty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Taizong. Ruoshui enlisted Chai Chengwu, Zong Du, Wu Shu, and Yang Yi as co-compilers, and they produced eighty juan.

sentences.zh: 真宗覽書流涕，錫賚有差。

translations.literal: Zhenzong perused the book and shed tears; rewards and gifts were distributed in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong read the work he wept, and rewards were distributed in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗有畜犬甚馴，常在乘輿左右。

translations.literal: Earlier, Taizong had kept a dog that was very tame and was often at the side of the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong had once kept a remarkably tame dog that was always at his side when he rode in the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 及崩，嗚號不食，因送永熙陵寢。

translations.literal: When Taizong died, it howled and wailed and would not eat, and was therefore sent to the Yongxi mausoleum precinct.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, the dog wailed and refused food, and was therefore sent to remain at the Yongxi mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 李至嘗詠其事，欲若水書之以戒浮俗，若水不從。

translations.literal: Li Zhi once versified this affair and wanted Ruoshui to write it out as a warning against shallow custom; Ruoshui would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi once composed a poem about the incident and asked Ruoshui to inscribe it as a rebuke to shallow fashion, but Ruoshui refused.

sentences.zh: 呂端雖為監修，以不蒞局不得署名，至抉其事以為專美。

translations.literal: Although Lü Duan was supervising compiler, because he did not attend the bureau he could not sign his name; Li Zhi seized on this matter, claiming Ruoshui was monopolizing credit.
translations.idiomatic: Although Lü Duan was titular supervising compiler, he had not actually attended the bureau and therefore could not sign the work; Li Zhi seized on this and accused Ruoshui of hogging the credit.

sentences.zh: 若水稱詔旨及唐朝故事以折之，時議不能奪。

translations.literal: Ruoshui cited imperial instructions and Tang-dynasty precedent to refute him, and contemporary opinion could not overturn his position.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui cited imperial instructions and Tang precedent in rebuttal, and public opinion could not overturn him.

sentences.zh: 既又重修《太祖實錄》，參以王禹偁、李宗諤、梁顥、趙安仁，未周歲畢。

translations.literal: Thereafter he again revised the Veritable Records of Taizu, with Wang Yucheng, Li Zong'e, Liang Hao, and Zhao Anren participating; it was completed in less than a year.
translations.idiomatic: He next oversaw a new compilation of the Veritable Records of Emperor Taizu, with Wang Yucheng, Li Zong'e, Liang Hao, and Zhao Anren as collaborators, and finished within the year.

sentences.zh: 安仁時為宗正卿，上言夔王於太宗屬當為兄，《實錄》所紀繆誤。

translations.literal: Anren was then director of the Imperial Clan Court; he submitted a memorial that Prince Kui, in relation to Taizong, should rank as elder brother, and that what the Veritable Records recorded was erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Anren was director of the Imperial Clan Court. He memorialized that Prince Kui, in genealogical relation to Emperor Taizong, ought to be recorded as his elder brother, and that the Veritable Records were in error.

sentences.zh: 若水援國初詔令，廷諍數四乃定。

translations.literal: Ruoshui cited early founding edicts and remonstrated in court several times before the matter was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui cited founding-era edicts and argued the point repeatedly at court before the matter was finally settled.

sentences.zh: 俄判吏部流內銓。

translations.literal: Soon he served as administrator of the Ministry of Personnel's flowing-within selection board.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took charge of the flowing-within selection board in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 從幸大名，若水陳禦敵安邊之策，有曰：

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor on a visit to Daming, Ruoshui set forth a strategy for repelling enemies and securing the frontier, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Daming, Ruoshui presented a plan for defending against the enemy and securing the border. He said:

sentences.zh: 「孫武著書，以伐謀為主；

translations.literal: 'In Sun Wu's book, attacking stratagems is taken as primary;
translations.idiomatic: "In Sun Wu's Art of War, the supreme aim is to overcome the enemy's plans;

sentences.zh: 漢高將將，以用法為先。

translations.literal: when Emperor Gaozu of Han employed generals, enforcing law came first.
translations.idiomatic: when Emperor Gaozu of Han employed his generals, he put enforcing discipline first.

sentences.zh: 伐謀者，以將帥能料敵制勝也；

translations.literal: Attacking stratagems means that commanders can anticipate the enemy and secure victory;
translations.idiomatic: To overcome the enemy's plans means that commanders can anticipate the foe and win;

sentences.zh: 用法者，以朝廷能賞罰不私也。

translations.literal: enforcing law means that the court can reward and punish without partiality.
translations.idiomatic: to enforce discipline means that the court can reward and punish without favoritism.

sentences.zh: 今傅潛領雄師數萬，閉門不出，坐視邊寇俘掠生民，上孤委注之恩，下挫銳師之氣，蓋潛輩不能制勝，朝廷未能用法使然也。

translations.literal: Now Fu Qian commands tens of thousands of elite troops yet keeps the gates shut and will not go out, sitting by while frontier raiders seize and plunder the people—above he fails the grace of entrustment, below he crushes the spirit of crack troops. This is because men like Qian cannot secure victory, and the court has been unable to enforce the law.
translations.idiomatic: Today Fu Qian commands tens of thousands of crack troops yet keeps his gates shut and will not march out, standing by while border raiders seize and plunder the people. Above, he betrays the trust placed in him; below, he crushes the morale of a sharp army. The reason is that commanders like Qian cannot win battles, and the court has failed to enforce military law.

sentences.zh: 軍法，臨陣不用命者斬。

translations.literal: Military law states that whoever disobeys orders on the battlefield is to be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Military law decrees that whoever disobeys orders in battle is to be executed.

sentences.zh: 今若斬潛以徇，然後擢如楊延朗、楊嗣者五七人，增其爵秩，分授兵柄，使將萬人，間以強弩，分路討除，孰敢不用命哉？

translations.literal: If Qian were now beheaded as an example, and then five or seven men such as Yang Yanlang and Yang Si were promoted, their ranks and titles increased, and military authority divided among them so that each commanded ten thousand men, with powerful crossbows deployed between them and punitive expeditions sent by separate routes—who would dare disobey orders?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty were to execute Qian as an example, then promote five or seven officers such as Yang Yanlang and Yang Si, raise their ranks, and divide command among them so that each leads ten thousand men, with strong crossbows deployed between columns and punitive columns sent by separate routes—who would dare disobey?

sentences.zh: 敵人聞我將帥不用命，退則有死，豈獨思遁，抑亦來歲不敢犯邊矣。

translations.literal: When the enemy hears that our commanders who disobey orders die in retreat, will they not only think of flight, but also not dare violate the border next year?
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy learns that our commanders who fail in battle die for it, they will not only think of fleeing, but will not dare raid the border the following year either.

sentences.zh: 如此則可以坐清邊塞，然後鑾輅還京，天威懾於四海矣。

translations.literal: In this way the frontier passes can be cleared while seated; then the imperial carriage may return to the capital, and Heaven's majesty will awe the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the border can be pacified without further exertion, the imperial carriage can return to the capital, and the imperial majesty will awe all within the four seas.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗讀前史，周世宗即位之始，劉崇結敵入寇，敵遣其將楊衮領騎兵數萬，隨崇至高平。

translations.literal: Your servant has read the former histories. At the beginning of Emperor Shizong of Zhou's accession, Liu Chong allied with the enemy to invade. The enemy sent his general Yang Gun at the head of tens of thousands of cavalry, following Chong to Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: I have read the former histories. At the beginning of Emperor Shizong of Zhou's accession, Liu Chong allied with the enemy to invade. The enemy sent his general Yang Gun at the head of tens of thousands of cavalry, following Chong to Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 當時懦將樊愛能、何徽等臨敵不戰，世宗大陳宴會，斬愛能等，拔偏將十餘人，分兵擊太原。

translations.literal: At that time the cowardly generals Fan Aineng, He Hui, and others faced the enemy but would not fight. Shizong held a great banquet, beheaded Aineng and the others, promoted more than ten lower generals, and divided his forces to strike Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the cowardly generals Fan Aineng, He Hui, and others faced the enemy but would not fight. Shizong held a great banquet, beheaded Aineng and the others, promoted more than ten lower generals, and divided his forces to strike Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 劉崇聞之，股慄不敢出，即日遁去。

translations.literal: When Liu Chong heard of this, he trembled with fear and dared not come out, fleeing that same day.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chong heard of this, he trembled with fear and dared not come out, fleeing that same day.

sentences.zh: 自是兵威大振。

translations.literal: From then on military prestige shook greatly.
translations.idiomatic: From then on military prestige shook greatly.

sentences.zh: 其後收淮甸，下秦、鳳，平關南，特席卷爾。

translations.literal: Afterward he recovered the Huainan region, took Qin and Feng, pacified Guannan—it was simply a sweeping conquest.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he recovered the Huainan region, took Qin and Feng, pacified Guannan—it was simply a sweeping conquest.

sentences.zh: 以陛下之神武，豈讓世宗乎？

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's divine martial prowess, would you yield to Shizong?
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's divine martial prowess, would you yield to Shizong?

sentences.zh: 此今日禦敵之奇策也。

translations.literal: This is the extraordinary stratagem for repelling the enemy today.
translations.idiomatic: This is the extraordinary stratagem for repelling the enemy today.

sentences.zh: 若將來安邊之術，請以近事言之，太祖朝制置最得其宜。

translations.literal: As for future methods of securing the frontier, I ask leave to speak from recent events: the arrangements of Taizu's reign attained the balance most fitting.
translations.idiomatic: As for how to secure the frontier in the future, let me speak from recent experience: the arrangements of Emperor Taizu's reign were the most apt.

sentences.zh: 止以郭進在邢州，李漢超在關南，何繼筠在鎮定，賀惟忠在易州，李謙溥在隰州，姚內斌在慶州，董遵誨在通遠軍，王彥昇在原州，但授緣邊巡檢之名，不加行營部署之號，率皆十餘年不易其任。

translations.literal: Guo Jin alone was at Xingzhou, Li Hanchao at Guannan, He Jijun at Zhending, He Weizhong at Yizhou, Li Qianbo at Xizhou, Yao Neibin at Qingzhou, Dong Zunhui at Tongyuan Army, and Wang Yansheng at Yuanzhou—only the title of frontier inspector was granted, without adding the designation of campaign deployment commander, and for the most part their posts were not changed for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu stationed Guo Jin at Xingzhou, Li Hanchao at Guannan, He Jijun at Zhending, He Weizhong at Yizhou, Li Qianbo at Xizhou, Yao Neibin at Qingzhou, Dong Zunhui at Tongyuan Army, and Wang Yansheng at Yuanzhou. He gave them only the title of frontier inspector, not that of campaign deployment commander, and for the most part left them in post for more than ten years without change.

sentences.zh: 立邊功者厚加賞賚，其位皆不至觀察使。

translations.literal: Those who established frontier merit received generous rewards and gifts, yet none of their posts reached that of observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Those who won frontier merit received generous rewards, yet none of them rose as high as observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 蓋位不高則朝廷易製，任不易則邊事盡知。

translations.literal: Because rank was not high, the court could control them easily; because tenure was not changed, frontier affairs were fully known.
translations.idiomatic: Because their rank was not high, the court could control them easily; because their appointments were stable, frontier affairs were thoroughly understood.

sentences.zh: 然後授以聖謀，來則掩殺，去則勿追，所以十七年中，北邊、西蕃不敢犯塞，以至屢使乞和，此皆陛下之所知也。

translations.literal: Then they were entrusted with the sage strategy: when the enemy came, ambush and strike; when they departed, do not pursue. Thus for seventeen years the northern frontier and the western Tibetans did not dare violate the passes, until they repeatedly sent envoys suing for peace—all of which Your Majesty knows.
translations.idiomatic: They were then entrusted with the emperor's strategy: strike when the enemy came, but do not pursue when they withdrew. For seventeen years the northern tribes and the western Tibetans did not dare breach the passes, until they repeatedly sent envoys suing for peace—all of which Your Majesty well knows.

sentences.zh: 苟能遵太祖故事，慎擇名臣，分理邊郡；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can follow Taizu's precedents, carefully select renowned ministers, and divide administration of the frontier prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will follow Emperor Taizu's precedent, carefully choose distinguished ministers, and divide the administration of the frontier prefectures among them;

sentences.zh: 罷部署之號，使不相統轄；

translations.literal: abolish the title of deployment commander so that they do not command one another;
translations.idiomatic: abolish the title of deployment commander so that they do not stand over one another;

sentences.zh: 置巡檢之名，俾遞相救應。

translations.literal: establish the name of inspector so that they may relieve one another in succession.
translations.idiomatic: restore the title of inspector so that they may come to one another's aid in turn.

sentences.zh: 如此則出必擊寇，入則守城，不數年間，可致邊烽罷警矣。」

translations.literal: In this way, going out they will surely strike the raiders, coming in they will hold the cities, and within a few years the frontier beacon fires can cease their alarms.'
translations.idiomatic: In this way they will strike the enemy when they go out and hold the cities when they come in, and within a few years the frontier beacons can fall silent."

sentences.zh: 俄知開封府。

translations.literal: Soon he was made prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 時北邊未寧，內出手劄訪若水以策。

translations.literal: At the time the northern frontier was not yet settled; the emperor personally wrote a note asking Ruoshui for strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The northern frontier was still unsettled, and the emperor sent Ruoshui a personal note asking for his counsel.

sentences.zh: 若水陳備邊之要有五：一曰擇郡守；

translations.literal: Ruoshui set forth five essentials for securing the frontier: first, select prefects;
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui set forth five essentials for defending the frontier. First, select prefects;

sentences.zh: 二曰募鄉兵；

translations.literal: second, recruit local militia;
translations.idiomatic: second, recruit local militia;

sentences.zh: 三曰積芻粟；

translations.literal: third, accumulate fodder and grain;
translations.idiomatic: third, stockpile fodder and grain;

sentences.zh: 四曰革將帥；

translations.literal: fourth, reform commanders;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, reform the command structure;

sentences.zh: 五曰明賞罰。

translations.literal: fifth, clarify rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: fifth, make rewards and punishments clear.

sentences.zh: 「何謂擇郡守？

translations.literal: 'What is meant by selecting prefects?
translations.idiomatic: "What does it mean to select prefects?

sentences.zh: 今之所患，患在戰守不同心。

translations.literal: The present trouble lies in the fact that campaigning and defending are not of one mind.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble today is that the field commanders and the garrison commanders do not act in concert.

sentences.zh: 望陛下選沉厚有謀諳邊事者，任為邊郡刺史，令兼緣邊巡檢，許召勇敢之士為隨身部曲。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will select men who are steady, deep, resourceful, and versed in frontier affairs, appoint them prefects of frontier commanderies, have them concurrently hold frontier inspector posts, and permit them to recruit brave men as personal retinue troops.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty choose men who are steady, shrewd, and experienced in frontier affairs, appoint them prefects of border commanderies with concurrent duty as frontier inspectors, and allow them to recruit brave men as personal retinues.

sentences.zh: 廩贍不充則官為支給。

translations.literal: If provisions are insufficient, let the government supply them.
translations.idiomatic: If their rations fall short, let the government make up the difference.

sentences.zh: 然後嚴亭障，明斥候，每得事宜，密相報示。

translations.literal: Then tighten border posts and beacons, clarify scouts and sentries, and whenever circumstances warrant, secretly inform one another.
translations.idiomatic: Then tighten the border posts and beacons, keep scouts and sentries alert, and whenever anything significant occurs, share intelligence in secret.

sentences.zh: 寇來則互為救應，齊出討除；

translations.literal: When raiders come, they should rescue one another and sally forth together to suppress them;
translations.idiomatic: When raiders come, they should aid one another and march out together to drive them off;

sentences.zh: 寇去則不令遠追，各務安靜。

translations.literal: when raiders depart, do not order distant pursuit; each should keep to quiet defense.
translations.idiomatic: when the raiders withdraw, do not order distant pursuit, but let each post keep its peace.

sentences.zh: 苟無大過，勿為替移；

translations.literal: If there are no major faults, do not replace them;
translations.idiomatic: So long as they commit no serious fault, do not transfer them;

sentences.zh: 儻立微功，就加爵賞。

translations.literal: if they achieve even slight merit, immediately add rank and reward.
translations.idiomatic: if they win even modest merit, promote and reward them at once.

sentences.zh: 如此則戰守必能同心，敵人不敢近塞矣。

translations.literal: In this way campaigning and defending will surely be of one mind, and the enemy will not dare approach the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the field and garrison forces will surely act as one, and the enemy will not dare approach the border passes.

sentences.zh: 何謂募鄉兵？

translations.literal: What is meant by recruiting local militia?
translations.idiomatic: What does it mean to recruit local militia?

sentences.zh: 今之所患，患在不知敵情。

translations.literal: The present trouble lies in not knowing the enemy's situation.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble today is that we do not know the enemy's movements.

sentences.zh: 望詔逐州沿邊民為招收軍，給與糧賜，蠲其賦租。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will order the people along the frontier in each prefecture to be recruited as reception armies, given grain and gifts, and exempted from tax and rent.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty order the frontier peoples of each prefecture enrolled as local defense forces, grant them rations and stipends, and exempt them from taxes and corvée.

sentences.zh: 彼兩地之中，各有親族，使其懷惠，來布腹心。

translations.literal: Between those two regions each has kin; let them cherish favor and come to spread their innermost knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: On both sides of the border people have kin among the enemy; if we treat them generously, they will bring us intelligence from the heart of the foe.

sentences.zh: 彼若舉兵，此必預知，苟能預知，則百戰百勝矣。

translations.literal: If the enemy raises troops, this side will surely know beforehand; if one can know beforehand, then in a hundred battles one wins a hundred victories.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy mobilizes, we will know in advance; and if we know in advance, we will prevail in every engagement.

sentences.zh: 何謂積芻粟？

translations.literal: What is meant by accumulating fodder and grain?
translations.idiomatic: What does it mean to stockpile fodder and grain?

sentences.zh: 今之所患，患在困民力。

translations.literal: The present trouble lies in exhausting the people's strength.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble today is that the people's strength is being exhausted.

sentences.zh: 望陛下令緣邊各廣營田，以州郡長官兼其使額，每歲秋夏，較其課程，立鼓旗以齊之，行賞罰以勸之。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will order broad garrison farming along the frontier, with prefectural and commandery chiefs concurrently holding the commissioner titles; each year in autumn and summer compare their quotas, set up drums and banners to align them, and apply rewards and punishments to encourage them.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty order expanded military farming along the frontier, with prefectural chiefs serving concurrently as farming commissioners. Each year in autumn and summer compare their yields, set drums and banners to organize them, and apply rewards and punishments to spur them on.

sentences.zh: 仍縱商人入粟緣邊。

translations.literal: Also allow merchants to bring grain into the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Also allow merchants to transport grain to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 儻鎮戍有三年之備，則敵人不敢動矣。

translations.literal: If garrison posts have three years' provisions, then the enemy will not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: If the frontier garrisons hold three years' supplies, the enemy will not dare move against us.

sentences.zh: 何謂革將帥？

translations.literal: What is meant by reforming commanders?
translations.idiomatic: What does it mean to reform the command structure?

sentences.zh: 今之所患，患在重兵居外，輕兵居內。

translations.literal: The present trouble lies in heavy troops stationed outside and light troops stationed within.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble today is that the main army is posted abroad while the home garrisons are weak.

sentences.zh: 去歲傅潛以八萬騎屯中山，魏、博之間鎮兵全少，非鑾輅親征，則城邑危矣。

translations.literal: Last year Fu Qian encamped eighty thousand cavalry at Zhongshan; between Wei and Bo the garrison troops were altogether few—had the imperial carriage not marched in person, the cities would have been in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Last year Fu Qian kept eighty thousand cavalry at Zhongshan, while the garrisons between Wei and Bo were almost bare. Had the emperor not marched in person, the cities would have been lost.

sentences.zh: 望陛下慎選將臣任河北近鎮，仍依舊事節制邊兵，未能削部署之名，望且減行營之號；

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will carefully select generals and ministers to hold the near Hebei commands, still controlling frontier troops according to old practice; if the title of deployment commander cannot yet be abolished, I hope at least to reduce the designation of campaign headquarters;
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty carefully choose generals and ministers for the Hebei commands nearest the capital, and let them control frontier troops as in former times. If the title of deployment commander cannot yet be abolished, at least reduce the number of campaign headquarters;

sentences.zh: 有警則暫巡邊徼，無事則卻復舊藩。

translations.literal: when there is alarm they may temporarily patrol the frontier marches; when there is no affair they return to their former fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: when alarm comes they may temporarily patrol the border; when all is quiet they return to their regular posts.

sentences.zh: 豈惟不啟戎心，況復待勞以逸。

translations.literal: This would not only avoid arousing the enemy's martial intent, but moreover allow resting while the foe labors.
translations.idiomatic: This would not only avoid provoking the enemy, but let our troops rest while theirs grow weary.

sentences.zh: 如此則不失備邊之要，又無舉兵之名，且使重兵不屯一處，進退動靜，無施不可矣。

translations.literal: In this way the essentials of securing the frontier are not lost, there is no name of raising troops, and moreover heavy forces are not encamped in one place—advancing, retreating, moving, or resting, nothing cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: In this way we keep the essentials of frontier defense without the appearance of mobilizing for war, and the main army is not massed in one place, so that in advance or retreat, in movement or rest, nothing is impossible.

sentences.zh: 何謂明賞罰？

translations.literal: What is meant by clarifying rewards and punishments?
translations.idiomatic: What does it mean to make rewards and punishments clear?

sentences.zh: 今之所患，患在戎卒驕惰。

translations.literal: The present trouble lies in frontier soldiers' arrogance and indolence.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble today is that frontier troops have grown arrogant and slack.

sentences.zh: 臣自知府以來，見侍衛、殿前兩司送到邊上亡命軍卒，人數甚多。

translations.literal: Since I became prefect I have seen the two bureaus of the Palace and Hall guards send to the frontier a great many deserters from the army.
translations.idiomatic: Since I took office as prefect I have seen the Palace Guard and Hall Guard directorates send a great many deserters to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 臣試訊之，皆以思親為言，此蓋令之不嚴也。

translations.literal: When I questioned them, all spoke of longing for kin; this is surely because orders are not strict.
translations.idiomatic: When I questioned them, all said they missed their families. This shows that discipline is lax.

sentences.zh: 平時尚敢如此，況臨大敵乎？

translations.literal: If in normal times they still dare thus, how much more when facing a great enemy?
translations.idiomatic: If they dare behave so in peacetime, what will they do when they face a great enemy?

sentences.zh: 望陛下以此言示將帥，俾申嚴號令，以警其下。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will show this statement to commanders and have them enforce orders strictly to warn their subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty convey these words to the commanders and have them enforce their orders strictly as a warning to their men.

sentences.zh: 古人云：『賞不勸，謂之止善；

translations.literal: The ancients said: 'When rewards do not encourage, it is called stopping goodness;
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "When rewards fail to encourage, it is called stopping goodness;

sentences.zh: 罰不懲，謂之縱惡。』

translations.literal: when punishments do not chastise, it is called indulging evil.'
translations.idiomatic: when punishments fail to deter, it is called indulging evil."

sentences.zh: 又曰：『法不可移，令不可違。』

translations.literal: They also said: 'Law may not be shifted; orders may not be violated.'
translations.idiomatic: They also said, "Law must not be bent; orders must not be disobeyed."

sentences.zh: 臣嘗聞郭進出鎮西山，太祖每遣戍卒，必諭之曰：『汝等謹奉法。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that when Guo Jin went out to command the Western Hills, Taizu whenever he sent garrison troops would always instruct them, saying: 'You must carefully obey the law.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when Guo Jin took command of the Western Hills, whenever Taizu sent out garrison troops he would always warn them, "You must strictly obey the law.

sentences.zh: 我猶赦汝，郭進殺汝矣！』

translations.literal: I may still pardon you, but Guo Jin will kill you!'
translations.idiomatic: I may still spare you, but Guo Jin will have you executed!"

sentences.zh: 其假借如此，故郭進所至，未嘗少衄。

translations.literal: His delegated authority was such; therefore wherever Guo Jin went he never suffered the least setback.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the authority entrusted to him, and wherever Guo Jin went he never met with defeat.

sentences.zh: 陛下能鑒前日之事，即今日之元龜也。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can reflect on affairs of former days, that will be today's great tortoise oracle."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty can take the events of the past as your mirror, they will serve as the great precedent for today."

sentences.zh: 若水又言：「邊部用兵，唯視太白與月為進退者，誠以太白者將軍也，星辰者廷尉也。

translations.literal: Ruoshui further said: "When border districts employ troops, those who look only to Venus and the Moon for advance or retreat—truly Venus is the general and the stars are the minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui went on to say, "On the frontier, troops are moved according to the conjunction of Venus and the Moon—for Venus represents the general, and the stars represent the minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 合則有戰，不合則無戰；

translations.literal: When they conjoin there is battle; when they do not conjoin there is no battle;
translations.idiomatic: When they conjoin, there will be fighting; when they do not, there will be none;

sentences.zh: 合於東則主勝，合於西則客勝。

translations.literal: conjoin in the east and the host prevails; conjoin in the west and the guest prevails.
translations.idiomatic: if they conjoin in the east, the defender wins; if in the west, the invader wins.

sentences.zh: 陛下能用臣言以謹邊備，則邊部不召而自來矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can use your subject's words to keep border defenses strict, then border peoples will come without being summoned.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will heed my advice and keep the frontier defenses in good order, the border tribes will submit without being summoned.

sentences.zh: 太祖臨御十七年間，未嘗生事疆埸，而敵人往往遣使乞和者，以其任用得人而備禦有方也。

translations.literal: Throughout the seventeen years Taizu held the throne he never stirred trouble on the frontier, yet enemies often sent envoys begging peace—because he appointed capable men and had well-ordered defenses.
translations.idiomatic: During the seventeen years of Taizu's reign he never provoked trouble on the borders, yet enemies repeatedly sent envoys suing for peace—because he placed the right men in office and organized his defenses effectively.

sentences.zh: 陛下苟思兵者凶器，戰者危事，而不倒持太阿，授人以柄，則守在四夷，而常獲靜勝，此備禦之上策也。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty reflects that weapons are instruments of misfortune and war a perilous affair, and does not hold the sword Tai'e upside down handing another the hilt, then defense will lie with the four barbarians and you will constantly win without fighting—this is the finest strategy of border defense."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty bears in mind that arms are tools of calamity and war a dangerous undertaking, and does not hold the great sword Tai'e by the blade and hand another the hilt, then your defense will rest with the four quarters and you will win peace without fighting—this is the supreme strategy of frontier defense."

sentences.zh: 未幾，出知天雄軍兼兵馬部署。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as prefect of the Tianxiong Army and concurrently military deployment commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent out to serve as prefect of the Tianxiong Army and concurrent commissioner for troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 時言事者請城綏州，屯兵積穀以備党項。

translations.literal: At the time memorialists asked to fortify Suizhou, station troops and accumulate grain to guard against the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, officials submitting memorials urged that Suizhou be walled, garrisoned, and stocked with grain as a defense against the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 邊城互言利害，前後遣使數輩按視，不能決。

translations.literal: Border cities disputed advantages and drawbacks; envoys were sent repeatedly to inspect on the spot, yet no decision could be made.
translations.idiomatic: The border commanderies argued back and forth over the pros and cons, and although several missions were dispatched in succession to inspect the site, no decision could be reached.

sentences.zh: 時已大發丁夫，將興其役，詔若水自大名馳往視之。

translations.literal: Draft labor had already been widely mobilized and the project was about to begin; Ruoshui was ordered to ride post-haste from Daming to inspect it.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée labor had already been mobilized on a large scale and construction was about to begin, when an edict ordered Ruoshui to ride post-haste from Daming to inspect the project.

sentences.zh: 若水上言：「綏州頃為內地，民賦登集，尚須旁郡轉餉。

translations.literal: Ruoshui memorialized: "Suizhou was not long ago inland territory; though civilian taxes were collected there, it still needed neighboring prefectures to forward provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui submitted a memorial saying, "Suizhou was until recently an interior district. Even when its taxes were fully collected, it still had to rely on neighboring prefectures to forward supplies.

sentences.zh: 自賜地趙保忠以來，人戶凋殘，若復城之，即須增戍。

translations.literal: Since the land was granted to Zhao Baozhong the population has dwindled; if we rebuild the city we must increase garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Since the territory was granted to Zhao Baozhong, the population has declined sharply. If the city is rebuilt, garrisons must be increased as well.

sentences.zh: 芻糧之給，全仰河東。

translations.literal: Fodder and grain would depend entirely on Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Fodder and grain would have to come entirely from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 其地隔越黃河、鐵碣二山，無定河在其城下，緩急用兵，輸送艱阻。

translations.literal: The place is cut off by the Yellow River and the two Iron Jie mountains; the Wuding River lies below its walls—in urgent military need transport would be arduous.
translations.idiomatic: The terrain is cut off by the Yellow River and the two Iron Jie mountains, with the Wuding River flowing beneath the city walls. In an emergency, moving supplies for military use would be extremely difficult.

sentences.zh: 且其地險，若未葺未完，邊寇奔衝，難於固守。

translations.literal: Moreover the terrain is perilous; if repairs are not finished, border raiders may charge in and it will be hard to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the ground is treacherous. If the fortifications are not fully repaired before border raiders strike, the place will be hard to defend.

sentences.zh: 況城邑焚毀，片瓦不存，所過山林，材木匱乏。

translations.literal: Moreover the cities and towns were burned—not a tile remains—and along the route the mountain forests lack timber.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the towns have been burned to the ground, not a tile left standing, and the forests along the route are depleted of timber.

sentences.zh: 城之甚勞，未見其利。」

translations.literal: To build the city would be very laborious with no visible benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Rebuilding the city would cost enormous labor with no clear benefit to show for it."

sentences.zh: 復詣闕面陳其事，上嘉納之，遂罷役。

translations.literal: He again went to court to state the matter in person; the emperor praised and accepted it and stopped the project.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to court in person to present his views. The emperor praised and accepted his advice, and the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 初，若水率眾過河，分布軍伍，咸有節制，深為戍將推服。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ruoshui led troops across the river he distributed the forces with proper discipline, deeply impressing the garrison commanders who submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Ruoshui led his troops across the river, he deployed the units with strict discipline, winning the deep respect of the frontier commanders.

sentences.zh: 上謂左右曰：「若水，儒臣中知兵者也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to those around him: "Ruoshui is among the scholar-officials one who understands warfare."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remarked to those around him, "Of all the scholar-officials, Ruoshui is one who truly understands military affairs."

sentences.zh: 是秋，又遣巡撫陝西緣邊諸郡，令便宜制置邊事。

translations.literal: That autumn he was again sent to tour and reassure the border prefectures of Shaanxi, empowered to handle border affairs as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was again dispatched to tour and reassure the border prefectures of Shaanxi, with authority to handle frontier affairs as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 還拜鄧州觀察使、幷代經略使、知幷州事。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Dengzhou observer, commissioner for Bing and Dai, and prefect of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Observer of Dengzhou, Commissioner for Bing and Dai, and Prefect of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年春，因疾灸兩足，創潰出血數斗，自是體貌羸瘵，手詔慰勞之，俾歸京師。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year, because of illness he applied moxibustion to both feet; the sores ulcerated and several dou of blood flowed forth; thereafter his body grew wasted; an imperial handwritten edict comforted him and he was sent back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year he treated an illness with moxibustion on both feet; the wounds ulcerated and he lost several dou of blood. From then on his health declined sharply. The emperor sent a handwritten edict to comfort him and ordered him back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 數月，始赴朝謁，因與僚友會食僧舍，假寢而卒，年四十四。

translations.literal: Several months later he first attended court audience; while dining with colleagues at a monastery he lay down for a nap and died, aged forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he made his first appearance at court. While dining with colleagues at a Buddhist monastery, he lay down for a rest and died, at the age of forty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈戶部尚書，賜其母白金五百兩。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Revenue and his mother was given five hundred taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister of Revenue, and his mother was granted five hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 子延年，甫七歲，錄為太常奉禮郎。

translations.literal: His son Yannian, just seven years old, was enrolled as a ceremonial attendant of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yannian, only seven years old, was enrolled as a Ceremonial Attendant of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 若水美風神，有器識，能斷大事，事繼母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Ruoshui had fine bearing and presence, capacity and insight, could decide great affairs, and was known for filial devotion to his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui possessed a striking presence and sound judgment, could decide weighty matters, and was renowned for the filial devotion he showed his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 雅善談論，尤輕財好施。

translations.literal: He excelled in elegant discourse and was especially free with money and generous in giving.
translations.idiomatic: He was an engaging conversationalist and especially generous with his wealth.

sentences.zh: 所至推誠待物，委任僚佐，總其綱領，無不稱治。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he dealt with people in good faith, entrusted staff with tasks while he held the overall plan—everywhere he was said to govern well.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he treated people with sincerity, delegated tasks to his staff while keeping hold of the overall plan, and was everywhere praised for good governance.

sentences.zh: 汲引後進，推賢重士，襟度豁如也。

translations.literal: He lifted up juniors, esteemed the worthy and honored scholars, and his breadth of mind was open.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted younger talent, valued the worthy, and treated scholars with respect; his generosity of spirit was boundless.

sentences.zh: 精術數，知年壽不永，故懇避權位。

translations.literal: Skilled in divination and numbers, he knew his lifespan would not be long and therefore earnestly avoided high office.
translations.idiomatic: Proficient in divination, he knew his life would be short and therefore earnestly sought to avoid high office.

sentences.zh: 其死也，士君子尤惜之。

translations.literal: At his death scholar-gentry especially regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: At his death, men of learning and principle mourned him with particular sorrow.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 兄若愚，比部員外郎。

translations.literal: His elder brother Ruoyu was Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Ruoyu served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 從弟若冲，大中祥符中，調河陽令。

translations.literal: His cousin Ruochong, in the Dazhong Xiangfu era, was transferred to magistrate of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Ruochong was transferred to the post of magistrate of Heyang during the Dazhong Xiangfu period.

sentences.zh: 有僕酗酒，杖之百數。

translations.literal: A servant was drunk; he beat him a hundred-odd strokes.
translations.idiomatic: A servant came to him drunk, and he had him beaten more than a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 僕挾刀夜潛室中，斷其臂，若冲大呼；

translations.literal: The servant took a knife and at night stole into the chamber and severed his arm; Ruochong cried out loudly;
translations.idiomatic: The servant took a knife and crept into his room at night, severing his arm. Ruochong cried out in alarm;

sentences.zh: 又害其幼子。

translations.literal: and also killed his young son.
translations.idiomatic: the servant also killed his young son.

sentences.zh: 詔磔僕於其門。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the servant dismembered at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the servant dismembered at Ruochong's gate.

sentences.zh: 真宗念若水母老，遣使存問，賜緡、綿、羊、酒；

translations.literal: Zhenzong, mindful that Ruoshui's mother was old, sent an envoy to inquire after her and bestowed cash, cotton, sheep, and wine;
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong, mindful that Ruoshui's mother was elderly, sent an envoy to inquire after her welfare and bestowed cash, cotton, sheep, and wine;

sentences.zh: 且賜若冲帛三十端，補孟州別駕。

translations.literal: and also gave Ruochong thirty bolts of silk and appointed him Assistant Prefect of Mengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: and also granted Ruochong thirty bolts of silk and appointed him Assistant Prefect of Mengzhou.

sentences.zh: 延年後以獻文賜進士出身，歷太常博士、集賢校理。

translations.literal: Yannian later received jinshi status by presenting a literary work, and served as Doctor of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Yannian later received jinshi status by presenting a literary composition and served successively as Doctor of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 蘇易簡

translations.literal: Su Yijian
translations.idiomatic: Su Yijian

sentences.zh: 蘇易簡，字太簡，梓州銅山人。

translations.literal: Su Yijian, styled Taijian, was a native of Tongshan in Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yijian, styled Taijian, was a native of Tongshan in Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 父協，舉蜀進士，歸宋，累任州縣，以易簡居翰林，任開封縣兵曹參軍，俄遷光祿寺丞，卒，特贈秘書丞。

translations.literal: His father Xie passed the Shu jinshi examination, submitted to Song, served repeatedly in prefectures and counties; because Yijian was in the Hanlin Academy, Xie was made military affairs official of Kaifeng County, soon promoted Secretary Director of the Court for Imperial Sacrifices, died, and was specially posthumously made Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xie had passed the Shu jinshi examination and submitted to the Song. He served in several prefectural and county posts. Because Yijian held a post in the Hanlin Academy, Xie was appointed military affairs official of Kaifeng County, and soon after promoted to Director of the Court for Imperial Sacrifices. He died and was posthumously granted the title of Secretary Director.

sentences.zh: 易簡少聰悟好學，風度奇秀，才思敏贍。

translations.literal: Yijian in youth was clever and eager to learn, bearing wonderfully refined, talent quick and abundant.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Yijian was clever and eager to learn, with a striking bearing and quick, abundant talent.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年，年踰弱冠，舉進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, having passed weak capping age, he took the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, having passed the age of twenty, he entered the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 太宗方留心儒術，貢士皆臨軒覆試。

translations.literal: Taizong was then attentive to Confucian learning; all presented scholars underwent palace re-examination.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was then devoted to Confucian learning, and all candidates were re-examined before the throne.

sentences.zh: 易簡所試三千餘言立就，奏上，覽之稱賞，擢冠甲科。

translations.literal: Yijian's test composition of more than three thousand words was completed at once; submitted upward, on reading it was praised; he was placed first in the top grade.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian's examination essay of more than three thousand characters was completed on the spot. When it was submitted, the emperor read it with high praise and placed him first in the top grade.

sentences.zh: 解褐將作監丞，通判昇州，遷左讚善大夫。

translations.literal: On leaving office he was made Director of Palace Construction, transit prefect of Shengzhou, promoted Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving office he was appointed Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, made transit prefect of Shengzhou, and promoted to Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 八年，以右拾遺知制誥。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made Right Reminder and Document Drafting Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Right Reminder and charged with drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，以郊祀恩進秩祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi, by suburban sacrifice grace he was promoted to Bureau of Temples Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongxi era, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Temples by grace of the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 二年，與賈黃中同知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the second year he and Jia Huangzhong jointly supervised the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he and Jia Huangzhong jointly supervised the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 有詔，凡親屬就舉者，籍名別試。

translations.literal: There was an edict that wherever kin took the examination their names were registered for a separate test.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued that whenever a relative of an examiner took the examination, his name was to be registered and he was to sit for a separate test.

sentences.zh: 易簡妻弟崔範，匿父喪充貢，奏名在上第；

translations.literal: Yijian's wife's younger brother Cui Fan concealed his father's mourning to compete and was listed among top graduates;
translations.idiomatic: Yijian's brother-in-law Cui Fan concealed his father's death to sit for the examination and was ranked among the top graduates;

sentences.zh: 又王千里者，水部員外郎孚之子，協為孚門生，千里預薦。

translations.literal: Also one Wang Qianli, son of Vice Director of Works Wang Fu—Xie had been Fu's student—Qianli was recommended.
translations.idiomatic: also one Wang Qianli, son of Vice Director of the Ministry of Works Wang Fu. Xie had been Fu's student, and Qianli had been recommended through that connection.

sentences.zh: 上聞，坐範及千里罪。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, Fan and Qianli were punished.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, Fan and Qianli were punished.

sentences.zh: 易簡緣是罷知制誥，以本官奉朝請。

translations.literal: Yijian was therefore dismissed from drafting edicts, retaining his original rank as court attendee.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian was consequently dismissed from his post drafting edicts and retained only his original rank as a court attendee.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復知制誥。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made drafting drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored to his post drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 三年，充翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 初，易簡充貢，宋白掌貢部，至是裁七年。

translations.literal: Earlier when Yijian competed, Song Bai held the examination bureau—now it was only seven years.
translations.idiomatic: When Yijian first sat for the examination, Song Bai had headed the examination bureau—only seven years had passed since then.

sentences.zh: 易簡幼時隨父河南，賈黃中來使，嘗教之屬辭；

translations.literal: Yijian in youth followed his father to Henan; Jia Huangzhong came on mission and once taught him literary composition;
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Yijian had accompanied his father to Henan, where Jia Huangzhong came on an official visit and once taught him how to compose literary pieces;

sentences.zh: 及是，悉為同列。

translations.literal: now they were all colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: now they were all colleagues of equal rank.

sentences.zh: 易簡連知貢舉，陳堯叟、孫何並甲廷試。

translations.literal: Yijian successively supervised examinations; Chen Yaosou and Sun He both topped the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian supervised the metropolitan examination on several occasions, and Chen Yaosou and Sun He both placed first in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年，丁外艱。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunhua he mourned his father.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chunhua he entered mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 二年，同知京朝官考課，遷中書舍人，充承旨。

translations.literal: In the second year he jointly supervised capital official performance review, was promoted Secretariat Drafter, and made chief academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he jointly supervised the performance review of capital officials, was promoted to Secretariat Drafter, and appointed chief Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 先是，曲宴將相，翰林學士皆預坐，梁迥啟太祖罷之；

translations.literal: Earlier at informal banquets with chief ministers, Hanlin academicians all sat—Liang Jiong persuaded Taizu to end this;
translations.idiomatic: Previously, at informal banquets with chief ministers, Hanlin academicians had all been seated among them, until Liang Jiong persuaded Taizu to abolish the practice;

sentences.zh: 又皇帝御丹鳳樓，翰林承旨侍從升樓西南隅，禮亦廢。

translations.literal: Also when the emperor ascended Crimson Phoenix Tower, the Hanlin chief academician and attendants ascended the southwest corner—this rite too was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: also, when the emperor mounted the Crimson Phoenix Tower, the Hanlin chief academician and his attendants would ascend to the southwest corner of the tower—a ceremony that too had been discontinued.

sentences.zh: 至是，易簡請之，皆復舊制。

translations.literal: Now Yijian requested restoration and all old regulations were revived.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Yijian petitioned for their restoration, and all the old regulations were reinstated.

sentences.zh: 易簡續唐李肇《翰林志》二卷以獻，帝賜詩以嘉之。

translations.literal: Yijian continued Tang Li Zhao's "Hanlin Annals" in two juan and presented it; the emperor bestowed a poem in praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian continued Li Zhao of Tang's Hanlin Annals in two juan and presented it to the throne. The emperor bestowed a poem in praise.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗以輕綃飛白大書『玉堂之署』四字，令易簡牓於廳額。

translations.literal: The emperor once used light silk with flying-white script to write large characters "Hall of Jade Splendor" and had Yijian post them over the hall entrance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once wrote the four characters "Hall of Jade Splendor" in large flying-white script on fine silk and ordered Yijian to post them over the hall entrance.

sentences.zh: 易簡會韓伾、畢士安、李至等往觀。

translations.literal: Yijian gathered Han Yi, Bi Shi'an, Li Zhi and others to go view them.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian gathered Han Yi, Bi Shi'an, Li Zhi, and others to go view the inscription.

sentences.zh: 上聞，遣中使賜宴甚盛，至等各賦詩紀其事，宰相李昉等亦作詩頌美之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and sent a palace envoy to give a very grand feast; each composed poetry to record the affair; Chief Councillor Li Fang and others also wrote poetry praising it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he sent a palace envoy to host a lavish feast. Li Zhi and the others each composed a poem to commemorate the occasion, and Chief Councillor Li Fang and others also wrote poems in praise.

sentences.zh: 他日，易簡直禁中，以水試欹器。

translations.literal: Another day Yijian was on straight duty in the forbidden palace and tested the tipping vessel with water.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, while on duty in the inner palace, Yijian tested a tipping vessel with water.

sentences.zh: 上密聞之，因晚朝，問曰：「卿所玩得非欹器耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor secretly heard; at evening court he asked: "What you were playing with—is it not the tipping vessel?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of it in secret, and at the evening audience asked, "What you were playing with—was it not a tipping vessel?"

sentences.zh: 易簡曰：「然，江南徐邈所作也。」

translations.literal: Yijian said: "Yes—it was made by Xu Miao of Jiangnan."
translations.idiomatic: Yijian replied, "Yes—it was made by Xu Miao of Jiangnan."

sentences.zh: 命取試之，易簡奏曰：「臣聞日中則昃，月滿則虧，器盈則覆，物盛則衰。

translations.literal: He was ordered to fetch and test it; Yijian memorialized: "Your subject has heard that when the sun reaches zenith it declines, when the moon is full it wanes, when vessels are full they overturn, when things flourish they decay.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to fetch it and demonstrate. Yijian submitted: "I have heard that when the sun reaches its zenith it begins to decline, when the moon is full it begins to wane, when a vessel is full it overturns, and when things reach their peak they decay.

sentences.zh: 願陛下持盈守成，慎終如始，以固丕基，則天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will hold fullness and guard accomplishment, be cautious at the end as at the beginning, to secure the great foundation—then all under Heaven will be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty will hold fast to fullness and guard what has been achieved, being as cautious at the end as at the beginning, so as to secure the great foundation of the state—then all under Heaven will be greatly blessed."

sentences.zh: 會郊祀，充禮儀使。

translations.literal: At a suburban sacrifice he served as ritual commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban sacrifice he served as ritual commissioner.

sentences.zh: 先是，扈蒙建議以宣祖升配。

translations.literal: Earlier Hu Meng proposed raising Xuanzu in sacrifice pairing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hu Meng had proposed that Xuanzu be elevated to share in the imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 易簡引唐故事，請以宣祖、太祖同配。

translations.literal: Yijian cited Tang precedent and asked that Xuanzu and Taizu be paired together.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian cited Tang precedent and petitioned that Xuanzu and Taizu be honored together in the sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The petition was accepted.

sentences.zh: 知審官院，言初任京朝官未嘗歷州縣，不得擬知州、通判，，詔可。

translations.literal: As director of the Bureau of Review he said capital officials on first appointment who had never served in prefectures and counties might not be nominated prefect or transit prefect—the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: As director of the Bureau of Review, he proposed that capital officials on their first appointment who had never served in prefectures or counties should not be nominated as prefect or transit prefect. An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 改知審刑院，俄掌吏部選，遷給事中、參知政事。

translations.literal: He was shifted to director of the Bureau of Punishments, soon took charge of Ministry of Personnel selections, promoted Impartial in Affairs and Participant in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the Bureau of Punishments, soon took charge of Ministry of Personnel selections, and was promoted to Impartial in Affairs and Participant in Governance.

sentences.zh: 時趙昌言亦參知政事，與易簡不協，至忿爭上前，上皆優容之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhao Changyan was also Participant in Governance and not in harmony with Yijian—they even quarreled heatedly before the emperor, who treated both with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhao Changyan was also a Participant in Governance and was at odds with Yijian. They even quarreled heatedly before the emperor, who treated both with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 未幾，昌言出使劍南，中路命改知鳳翔府。

translations.literal: Before long Changyan went out as envoy to Jiannan; mid-route he was ordered changed to prefect of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Changyan was sent as envoy to Jiannan, but mid-journey he was ordered reassigned as prefect of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 明年，易簡亦以禮部侍郎出知鄧州，移陳州。

translations.literal: The next year Yijian also went out as Vice Minister of Rites prefect of Dengzhou, then shifted to Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yijian too was sent out as Vice Minister of Rites and prefect of Dengzhou, then transferred to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，卒，年三十九，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao he died, aged thirty-nine; posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao he died at the age of thirty-nine and was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 易簡外雖坦率，中有城府。

translations.literal: Outwardly Yijian seemed forthright but inwardly he had a strategist's depth.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Yijian appeared frank and open, but inwardly he was calculating.

sentences.zh: 由知制誥入為學士，年未滿三十。

translations.literal: From drafting edicts he entered as academician before thirty.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from drafting edicts to Hanlin academician before the age of thirty.

sentences.zh: 屬文初不達體要，及掌誥命，頗自刻勵。

translations.literal: His literary compositions at first did not grasp essentials; once he held charge of edicts he greatly disciplined himself.
translations.idiomatic: His early literary compositions did not grasp the essentials of the form, but once he took charge of drafting edicts he applied himself with great discipline.

sentences.zh: 在翰林八年，眷遇敻絕倫等。

translations.literal: Eight years in the Hanlin, favor surpassing all peers.
translations.idiomatic: During his eight years in the Hanlin Academy, the favor shown him far surpassed that accorded his peers.

sentences.zh: 李沆後入，在易簡下，先參知政事，故以易簡為承旨，錫賚均焉。

translations.literal: Li Hao entered later, was below Yijian, but became Participant in Governance first—for this Yijian was made chief academician and gifts were equal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hao entered the academy after Yijian and ranked below him, yet became Participant in Governance first. For this reason Yijian was made chief academician so that their gifts and honors would be equal.

sentences.zh: 太宗遵舊制，且欲稔其名望而後正臺輔，易簡以親老急於進用，因亟言時政闕失，遂參大政。

translations.literal: Taizong followed old system and also wished to ripen his reputation before making him chief minister; Yijian because his parents were old urgently sought advancement and therefore urgently spoke of present policy failures—thus entered great governance.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong followed the established practice of allowing a man's reputation to mature before appointing him to the highest offices. But Yijian, anxious to advance because his parents were elderly, repeatedly spoke out on failures in current policy and thus gained entry to the highest councils of state.

sentences.zh: 蜀人何光逢，易簡之執友也，嘗任縣令，坐賂削籍，流寓京師。

translations.literal: Shu man He Guangfeng, Yijian's close friend, had once been county magistrate, was demoted and struck from rolls for bribery, and drifted residing in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He Guangfeng of Shu, a close friend of Yijian, had once served as a county magistrate but was struck from the rolls and demoted for taking bribes, and was now living in exile in the capital.

sentences.zh: 會易簡典貢部，光逢代人充試以取貲，易簡於稠人中屏出之，光逢遂造謗書，斥言朝廷事，且譏易簡。

translations.literal: When Yijian was in charge of the Ministry of Rites examination bureau, Guangfeng had another person sit the examination in his place to obtain payment. Yijian had him expelled from among the dense crowd. Guangfeng thereupon composed a slanderous pamphlet, denouncing court affairs and also ridiculing Yijian.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Yijian directed the metropolitan examination, Guangfeng had someone take the test on his behalf for money. Yijian had him driven out of the throng. Guangfeng then wrote a libelous tract attacking court affairs and mocking Yijian as well.

sentences.zh: 易簡得其書以聞，逮捕光逢，獄具，坐棄市。

translations.literal: Yijian obtained the book and reported it upward. Guangfeng was arrested; when the case was complete, he was sentenced to execution in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian obtained the tract and reported it to the throne. Guangfeng was arrested, and when the investigation was complete he was executed in public.

sentences.zh: 易簡以殺光逢非其意，居常怏怏。

translations.literal: Yijian considered that Guangfeng's death had not been his intent, and at home he was often discontented.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian felt that Guangfeng's execution had not been what he intended, and he was often troubled in spirit.

sentences.zh: 母薛氏以殺父執切責之，易簡泣曰：「不謂及此，易簡罪也。」

translations.literal: His mother Lady Xue severely rebuked him for killing her husband's sworn brother. Yijian wept and said, "I did not expect it would come to this; the fault is Yijian's."
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Xue sharply rebuked him for killing her husband's sworn brother. Yijian wept and said, "I never thought it would come to this—the blame is mine."

sentences.zh: 及易簡參知政事，召薛氏入禁中，賜冠帔，命坐，問曰：「何以教子成此令器？」

translations.literal: When Yijian became Vice Grand Councilor, Lady Xue was summoned into the inner palace, granted cap and stole, and ordered to sit. The emperor asked, "By what means did you teach your son to become such an outstanding vessel?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yijian was appointed Vice Grand Councilor, Lady Xue was summoned to the inner palace, granted ceremonial cap and stole, and told to be seated. The emperor asked, "How did you raise your son to become such a fine man?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「幼則束以禮讓，長則教以詩書。」

translations.literal: She replied, "In youth I bound him with ritual and deference; in maturity I instructed him with the Classic of Poetry and the Book of Documents."
translations.idiomatic: She answered, "In childhood I restrained him with courtesy and yielding; when he grew older I taught him the Odes and the Documents."

sentences.zh: 上顧左右曰：「真孟母也。」

translations.literal: The emperor turned to those beside him and said, "A true Mother Meng indeed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked to those around him and said, "She is a true Mother Meng."

sentences.zh: 易簡性嗜酒，初入翰林，謝日飲已微醉，餘日多沉湎。

translations.literal: Yijian was by nature fond of wine. When he first entered the Hanlin Academy, on the day of his thanksgiving audience he had already drunk until slightly intoxicated; on remaining days he was often deeply submerged in drink.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian was naturally addicted to wine. When he first entered the Hanlin Academy, on the day of his audience of thanks he was already slightly drunk, and on most other days he drank to excess.

sentences.zh: 上嘗戒約深切，且草書《勸酒》二章以賜，令對其母讀之。

translations.literal: The emperor once admonished him earnestly and in addition drafted in cursive two chapters of "Exhortation against Wine" to bestow, ordering him to read them before his mother.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once warned him sternly and also wrote out in cursive two chapters of "Exhortation against Wine" as a gift, instructing him to read them to his mother.

sentences.zh: 自是每入直，不敢飲。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever he entered duty he did not dare to drink.
translations.idiomatic: After that, whenever he went on palace duty he did not dare to drink.

sentences.zh: 及卒，上曰：「易簡果以酒死，可惜也。」

translations.literal: When he died, the emperor said, "Yijian indeed died from wine—a pity."
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the emperor said, "Yijian truly drank himself to death. What a pity."

sentences.zh: 易簡常居雅善筆劄，尤善談笑，旁通釋典，所著《文房四譜》、《續翰林志》及《文集》二十卷，藏於秘閣。

translations.literal: Yijian constantly dwelt in refinement and excelled at letters, especially skilled at witty talk, and was broadly versed in Buddhist scriptures. His works—"Four Treatises on the Scholar's Studio," "Continuation of the Hanlin Chronicle," and a collected writings in twenty juan—were stored in the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian lived in elegant refinement and excelled at correspondence, especially at witty conversation, and was also well versed in Buddhist texts. His "Four Treatises on the Scholar's Studio," "Continuation of the Hanlin Chronicle," and a twenty-juan collected works were kept in the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 三子，曰宿、曰壽、曰耆，大中祥符間，皆祿之以官云。

translations.literal: He had three sons, named Su, Shou, and Qi; during the Dazhong Xiangfu era they were all granted salaries with official posts.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons—Su, Shou, and Qi—and during the Dazhong Xiangfu period they were all granted official salaries.

sentences.zh: 郭贄，字仲儀，開封襄邑人。

translations.literal: Guo Zhi, styled Zhongyi, was a native of Xiangyi in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhi, styled Zhongyi, was a native of Xiangyi in Kaifeng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，舉進士，中首薦。

translations.literal: In the Qiande era he presented himself as a jinshi candidate and placed first in the regional recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiande period he entered the jinshi examination and ranked first among the recommended candidates.

sentences.zh: 太宗尹京，因事藩邸。

translations.literal: When Taizong was administering the capital, Zhi entered his service in the princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Taizong was administering the capital, Zhi entered his service at the princely mansion.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，擢為著作佐郎、右讚善大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taiping Xingguo era he was promoted to Assistant in the Office for Writing and Right Attendant-in-Waiting for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Taiping Xingguo era he was promoted to Assistant in the Office for Writing and Right Attendant-in-Waiting for the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 俄兼皇子侍講，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he concurrently served as Lecturer to the Imperial Princes and was granted the scarlet robe and fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was also made lecturer to the imperial princes and granted the scarlet robe and fish tally.

sentences.zh: 太宗至東宮，出《戒子篇》，命贄注解，且令委曲講說，以喻諸王。

translations.literal: The emperor came to the Eastern Palace, produced the "Admonition to Sons" chapter, ordered Zhi to annotate it, and furthermore directed him to expound it fully in order to instruct all the princes.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong came to the Eastern Palace, produced the "Admonition to Sons," and ordered Zhi to annotate it and explain it thoroughly so as to instruct all the princes.

sentences.zh: 三年，與劉兼、張洎、王克正同知貢舉，遷右補闕，與宋白並拜中書舍人，賜金紫。

translations.literal: In the third year he served jointly with Liu Jian, Zhang Ji, and Wang Kezheng as directors of the metropolitan examination; he was transferred to Right Remonstrator and, together with Song Bai, was appointed jointly as Secretariat Drafters, granted the gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he served with Liu Jian, Zhang Ji, and Wang Kezheng as directors of the metropolitan examination, was promoted to Right Remonstrator, and together with Song Bai was appointed Secretariat Drafter and granted the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 五年，復與程羽、侯陟、宋白同知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again served with Cheng Yu, Hou Zhi, and Song Bai as directors of the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he again directed the metropolitan examination together with Cheng Yu, Hou Zhi, and Song Bai.

sentences.zh: 置京朝官差遣院，凡將命出入、受代歸闕官，悉考校勞績，銓量才品，命贄、洎、滕中正、雷德驤領之。

translations.literal: The Office for Assignment of Metropolitan Officials was established; for all officials going out or returning on imperial commission or succeeding to office and returning to court, their merits were altogether examined and their talent weighed, and Zhi, Ji, Teng Zhongzheng, and Lei Deqiang were appointed to lead it.
translations.idiomatic: The Office for Assignment of Metropolitan Officials was established. For every official sent out on commission, returning after completing a tour, or coming back to court after succession, merit was reviewed and talent weighed, and Zhi, Ji, Teng Zhongzheng, and Lei Deqiang were put in charge.

sentences.zh: 七年，以本官參知政事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, with his existing office he became Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became Vice Grand Councilor while retaining his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 曹彬為弭德超所誣，贄極言救解，深為宰相趙普所重。

translations.literal: When Cao Bin was slandered by Mi Dechao, Zhi spoke forcefully to secure his release and was deeply esteemed by Grand Councilor Zhao Pu.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Bin was framed by Mi Dechao, Zhi spoke out forcefully to save him and won the deep regard of Grand Councilor Zhao Pu.

sentences.zh: 嘗因論事奏曰：「臣受不次之遇，誓以愚直上報。」

translations.literal: Once when discussing affairs he memorialized, saying, "Your servant has received an extraordinary elevation and vows to repay it with blunt straightforwardness."
