translations.idiomatic: Once, while discussing policy, he submitted a memorial saying, "I have received an exceptional promotion and swear to repay it with blunt honesty."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「愚直何益於事？」

translations.literal: Taizong said, "What benefit does blunt straightforwardness bring to affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "What good does blunt honesty do for governing?"

sentences.zh: 贄言：「雖然，猶勝姦邪。」

translations.literal: Zhi said, "Even so, it is still better than treacherous wickedness."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi replied, "Even so, it is still better than treachery."

sentences.zh: 無何，以入對宿酲未解，左遷秘書少監、知荊南府。

translations.literal: Before long, because when entering audience his overnight hangover had not cleared, he was demoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and made prefect of Jingnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, because he entered audience while still suffering from the previous night's wine, he was demoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and appointed prefect of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 府俗尚淫祀，屬久旱，盛陳禱雨之具。

translations.literal: The prefecture's custom favored licentious sacrifices; as there had been a long drought, rain-prayer implements were displayed in profusion.
translations.idiomatic: The region was given to extravagant cult worship. During a prolonged drought, rain-prayer paraphernalia were set out in great profusion.

sentences.zh: 贄始至，命悉撤去，投之江，不數日大雨。

translations.literal: When Zhi first arrived he ordered them all removed and cast into the river; within not several days great rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi first arrived he ordered everything removed and thrown into the river, and within a few days heavy rain fell.

sentences.zh: 就加左諫議大夫，入為鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: He was thereupon additionally promoted to Left Remonstrator and entered the capital as Salt and Iron Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon further promoted to Left Remonstrator and recalled to the capital as Salt and Iron Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時諸路積逋欠犯人，雖死猶繫其子孫。

translations.literal: At the time on various circuits accumulated arrears involved offenders; though dead, their sons and grandsons were still held liable.
translations.idiomatic: At that time accumulated debts on the circuits still bound offenders' families: even after a man died, his sons and grandsons remained liable.

sentences.zh: 贄條陳其事，多所蠲貸。

translations.literal: Zhi set forth the matter in detailed clauses, and many debts were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi laid out the problem in a detailed memorial, and many obligations were forgiven.

sentences.zh: 籍田，超拜工部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the plowing ceremony he was specially promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the ceremonial plowing of the sacred field he was specially promoted to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，知澶州，坐河決免所居官。

translations.literal: During the Chunhua era he governed Danzhou and, because of a breach in the Yellow River, was dismissed from his post.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua period he governed Danzhou, but was removed from office when the Yellow River broke its banks.

sentences.zh: 久之，起為給事中，復工部侍郎，知審官院、通進銀臺封駁司。

translations.literal: After a long while he was raised up as Censor-in-Chief, restored as Vice Minister of Works, and made director of the Bureau for Review of Appointments and the Memorials Gateway Silver Terrace Sealing and Rejection Office.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was recalled as Censor-in-Chief, again made Vice Minister of Works, and put in charge of the Bureau for Review of Appointments and the Memorials Gateway Silver Terrace Sealing and Rejection Office.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，拜刑部，出知天雄軍。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong took the throne, Zhi was appointed Vice Minister of Justice and sent out as military commissioner of Tianxiong.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong took the throne, Zhi was appointed Vice Minister of Justice and sent out as military commissioner of Tianxiong.

sentences.zh: 翌日，贄入對，懇辭。

translations.literal: The next day Zhi entered audience and earnestly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhi entered audience and earnestly declined.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「全魏之地，所寄尤重，卿宜亟去。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The territory of all Wei is entrusted with especial weight. You should go there at once."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The territory of all Wei is entrusted with especial weight. You should go there at once."

sentences.zh: 入判太常寺、吏部流內銓，加集賢院學士、判院事。

translations.literal: He entered to administer the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the flowing-within selection board of the Ministry of Personnel, and was additionally made academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and administrator of the institute.
translations.idiomatic: He entered to administer the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the flowing-within selection board of the Ministry of Personnel, and was additionally made academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and administrator of the institute.

sentences.zh: 知河南府，歸朝，獻詩自陳，進秩吏部，俄兼秘書監。

translations.literal: He governed Henan prefecture, returned to court, presented a poem stating his case, was advanced in rank within the Ministry of Personnel, and soon also served as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Henan prefecture, returned to court, presented a poem stating his case, was advanced in rank within the Ministry of Personnel, and soon also served as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，真宗未出閣，贄已授經，上嘗至其家；

translations.literal: Earlier, before Zhenzong had left the palace study, Zhi had already instructed him in the classics; the emperor had once come to his home.
translations.idiomatic: Long before Zhenzong left the palace school, Zhi had already taught him the classics, and the emperor had once visited his home.

sentences.zh: 後楊可法繼其任，上以為輔導不及贄，嘗稱贄純厚長者。

translations.literal: Later Yang Kefa succeeded to his post; the emperor considered his tutelage inferior to Zhi's and once praised Zhi as a pure, generous elder.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang Kefa succeeded him, but the emperor thought his instruction fell short of Zhi's and once praised Zhi as a sincere and generous elder.

sentences.zh: 至是，在秘府，屢賜對，詢訪舊事。

translations.literal: At this time, in the Imperial Library, he was repeatedly granted audiences and questioned about old affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Now, in the imperial archives, he was repeatedly granted audiences and asked about events of earlier days.

sentences.zh: 且愍其已老，特拜工部尚書、翰林侍讀學士，作詩賜之，有『啟發冲言曉典常』語。

translations.literal: Moreover, pitying his advanced age, he was specially appointed Minister of Works and Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting; a poem was composed and bestowed upon him, containing the line "Opening and enlightening the heir's words, making him understand canonical norms."
translations.idiomatic: Pitying his advanced age, the court specially appointed him Minister of Works and Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting, composed a poem in his honor, and granted it to him, including the line "Opening the heir's understanding of the classics and their norms."

sentences.zh: 東封，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: At the eastern feng sacrifice he was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the eastern feng sacrifice he was promoted to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 太宗在晉邸時，凡製篇詠，多令屬和。

translations.literal: When Taizong was in the Jin princely residence, whenever he composed verses he often had Zhi harmonize with them.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong was still in the Jin princely mansion, whenever he wrote poetry he often had Zhi compose matching verses.

sentences.zh: 真宗嘗訪其賜本，贄集為四卷以獻，詔獎之。

translations.literal: Zhenzong once inquired after the originals of those gifts; Zhi collected them into four juan and presented them, and an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong once asked after the originals of those poems. Zhi gathered them into four juan and presented them, and the emperor issued an edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年，卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 上以舊學之故，特親臨哭之，贈左僕射，諡文懿。

translations.literal: Because of their old teacher-student relation the emperor especially came in person to mourn him, posthumously appointing him Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and giving him the posthumous name Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: Because of their long teacher-student bond, the emperor came in person to mourn him, posthumously appointed him Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and gave him the posthumous title Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 錄其子昭度為大理寺丞，昭升、昭用並大理評事，昭允左讚善大夫。

translations.literal: His son Zhaodu was enrolled as an assistant in the Court of Judicial Review; Zhaosheng and Zhaoyong were both evaluators in the Court of Judicial Review; and Zhaoyun was made Left Attendant-in-Waiting for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhaodu was made an assistant in the Court of Judicial Review; Zhaosheng and Zhaoyong were both made evaluators in the same court; and Zhaoyun was appointed Left Attendant-in-Waiting for the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 贄屬文敏速而不雕刻，昭度集為三十卷上之，賜名《文懿集》。

translations.literal: Zhi's literary compositions were quick and fluent without excessive carving; Zhaodu collected them into thirty juan and presented them, and they were granted the title "Wenyi Collection."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi wrote swiftly and gracefully without overwrought ornament. Zhaodu collected his works into thirty juan and presented them, and the collection was given the title Wenyi Collection.

sentences.zh: 性溫和，頗能延譽時雋。

translations.literal: His nature was mild and gentle, and he was quite able to extend reputation to outstanding men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He was mild by nature and quite skilled at recommending talented men of his day.

sentences.zh: 宋白以文學沉下位，贄薦引之，遂同掌誥命。

translations.literal: Song Bai, though accomplished in letters, languished in low position; Zhi recommended and introduced him, and they then jointly held the drafting of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Song Bai was accomplished in literature but languished in a low post until Zhi recommended him; the two then served together drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 趙昌言兒時，一見器之，及掌貢部，以為奏名之首，後卒貴顯。

translations.literal: When Zhao Changyan was a child, Zhi recognized his talent at first sight; when he directed the examination bureau he made him first in the submitted names, and he later attained high eminence.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Changyan was still a boy, Zhi recognized his promise at first meeting. Later, when Zhi directed the examinations, he placed Zhao first on the list, and Zhao eventually rose to high rank.

sentences.zh: 贄初充賦有聲，邑人同在籍中者忌之，潛加構毀，自是連上不中選。

translations.literal: When Zhi first took the examination he had a famous reputation; fellow townsmen on the same registry envied him and secretly slandered him, so from then on he repeatedly submitted but was not selected.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi first sat for the examinations he was already well known. Fellow townsmen on the same registry envied him and secretly slandered him, so he failed again and again.

sentences.zh: 洎贄再知貢舉，邑人子以明經充薦，詔下日，悔泣而去。

translations.literal: When Zhi again directed the metropolitan examination, a townsmen's son presented himself as a mingjing candidate; on the day the edict was issued he wept in regret and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi again directed the metropolitan examination, a townsman's son qualified as a mingjing candidate. On the day the edict was issued he wept and left in shame.

sentences.zh: 贄聞之，命其所親召還，慰諭俾就舉，遂預薦中第。

translations.literal: Zhi heard of it, ordered someone close to summon him back, comforted and urged him to take the examination, and he thereupon was recommended and passed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi heard of this he had a close associate bring the young man back, comforted him, and urged him to sit for the examination. He was recommended and passed.

sentences.zh: 然吝嗇，切於治生，晚節不事事，人頗以是少之。

translations.literal: Yet he was stingy and intent on managing livelihood; in his later years he did not attend to affairs, and people somewhat despised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was miserly and obsessed with managing his household. In his later years he neglected public business, and people looked down on him for it.

sentences.zh: 李至，字言幾，真定人。

translations.literal: Li Zhi, styled Yanji, was a native of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi, styled Yanji, was a native of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 母張氏，嘗夢八仙人自天降，授字圖使吞之，及寤，猶若有物在胸中，未幾，生至。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Zhang once dreamed that eight immortals descended from heaven, handed her a chart of characters to swallow, and upon waking still felt as if something remained in her breast; before long she gave birth to Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Zhang once dreamed that eight immortals descended from heaven and gave her a chart of characters to swallow. When she awoke she still felt as though something remained in her chest, and not long afterward she gave birth to Zhi.

sentences.zh: 七歲而孤，鞠於飛龍使李知審家。

translations.literal: Orphaned at seven, he was nurtured in the household of the Flying Dragon envoy Li Zhongshen.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at seven, he was raised in the household of the Flying Dragon envoy Li Zhongshen.

sentences.zh: 幼沉靜好學，能屬文。

translations.literal: As a youth he was calm, still, fond of learning, and able to compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was quiet and studious and could already write essays.

sentences.zh: 及長，辭華典贍。

translations.literal: When grown, his diction was elegant and ample.
translations.idiomatic: When he matured, his writing was elegant and full.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，釋褐將作監丞，通判鄂州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, left his russet robes as an assistant in the Directorate of Imperial Construction, and was made administrative vice-prefect of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, took his first office as an assistant in the Directorate of Imperial Construction, and was made vice-prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 旋擢著作郎、直史館。

translations.literal: Shortly he was promoted to Gentleman of the Writing Office and given direct appointment to the History Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Gentleman of the Writing Office with a concurrent appointment in the History Academy.

sentences.zh: 會征太原，命督澤、潞芻糧，累遷右補闕、知制誥。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Taiyuan arose, he was ordered to supervise fodder and grain for Ze and Lu prefectures, and was repeatedly promoted to Right Remonstrator and Drafter of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against Taiyuan began, he was ordered to supervise fodder and grain in Ze and Lu, and was repeatedly promoted until he became Right Remonstrator and Drafter of Edicts.

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年，轉比部郎中，為翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue and made Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue and made a Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 冬，拜右諫議大夫、參知政事。

translations.literal: In winter he was appointed Right Remonstrator and Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was appointed Right Remonstrator and Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，加給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi he was given the additional title Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongxi era he was given the additional title of Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時議親征范陽，至上疏以為：「兵者凶器，戰者危事，用之之道，必務萬全。

translations.literal: When there was discussion of the emperor personally campaigning against Fanyang, Zhi submitted a memorial stating: "Arms are inauspicious instruments; battle is a perilous affair—the way to employ them must assuredly seek complete safety.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated a personal campaign against Fanyang, Zhi submitted a memorial arguing: "Weapons are instruments of ill omen and war a perilous undertaking; the way to use them must be to seek complete security.

sentences.zh: 幽州為敵右臂，王師所嚮，彼必拒張，攻城數萬，兵食倍之。

translations.literal: Youzhou is the enemy's right arm; wherever the imperial army turns, they will surely resist and deploy; to besiege a city requires tens of thousands, and military provisions double that.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou is the enemy's right arm. Wherever the imperial army advances, the foe is sure to resist in force. A siege requires tens of thousands of men, and provisions must be twice that number.

sentences.zh: 今日邊庾未充，況范陽之傍，坦無陵阜，去山既遠，取石尤難。

translations.literal: Today the border granaries are not filled; moreover beside Fanyang the land is flat without mound or hill, mountains are far distant, and obtaining stone is especially difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The border granaries are not yet full. Moreover, the country around Fanyang is flat, without hills or mounds; stone is far away and especially hard to obtain.

sentences.zh: 金湯之堅，必資機石，儻有未備，願且繕完。

translations.literal: The solidity of metal and moat must rely on catapults and projectiles; if there is anything not prepared, I beg that it first be repaired and completed.
translations.idiomatic: The strength of walls and moats depends on siege engines and stones. If anything is lacking, I beg that it be prepared first.

sentences.zh: 畜威養銳，觀釁以伐謀，更縱彌年，亦未為晚。

translations.literal: Store up awe and nourish sharpness, observe openings to frustrate their plans—even if allowed another full year, it would not yet be late.
translations.idiomatic: Store up strength, sharpen the army, watch for openings, and defeat the enemy's plans—even waiting another year would not be too late.

sentences.zh: 必若聖心獨斷，在於必行，則京師天下之本，陛下恭守宗廟，不離京國，示敵人以閑暇，慰億兆之仰望，策之上也。

translations.literal: If the sacred mind alone decides and insists on going, then the capital is the root of all under Heaven—Your Majesty reverently guarding the ancestral temples and not leaving the capital, showing the enemy leisure, comforting the gaze of the hundred millions, is the highest strategy.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty's mind is fixed and the campaign must go forward, then the capital is the foundation of the realm. To remain at court, guard the ancestral temples, show the enemy that we are unhurried, and reassure the people—that is the best plan.

sentences.zh: 大名，河朔之咽喉，或暫駐鑾輅，揚言自將，以壯軍威，策之中也。

translations.literal: Daming is the throat of Hebei; perhaps temporarily station the imperial carriage there, proclaiming that you will personally command, to strengthen military awe—that is the middle strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Daming is the gateway of Hebei. Your Majesty might temporarily station the imperial carriage there and announce that you will take command in person to bolster the army's morale—that is the second-best plan.

sentences.zh: 若乃遠提師旅，親抵邊陲，北有契丹之虞，南有中原之慮，則曳裾之懇切，斷鞅之狂愚，臣雖不肖，恥在二賢後也。」

translations.literal: As for personally leading the army far to the border, with Khitan threat in the north and central plains concern in the south, then compared with the earnest plea of dragging the robe and the rash folly of cutting the reins—though your servant is unworthy, he would be ashamed to rank behind those two worthies."
translations.idiomatic: But to lead the army in person to the frontier, with Khitan danger in the north and anxiety for the central plains in the south, is to invite the earnest remonstrance of those who seized the emperor's robe and the reckless folly of those who cut the chariot reins. Though I am unworthy, I would be ashamed to fall short of those two loyal counselors."

sentences.zh: 至以目疾累表求解機政，授禮部侍郎，進秩吏部。

translations.literal: Zhi, because of eye illness, repeatedly memorialized requesting release from governing affairs; he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites and advanced in rank to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Because of eye trouble Zhi repeatedly asked to be relieved of governing duties. He was made Vice Minister of Rites and then promoted within the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 會建秘閣，命兼秘書監，選三館書置閣中，俾至總之。

translations.literal: When the Secret Archives were established, he was ordered concurrently to serve as Director of the Secretariat and to select books from the Three Institutes to place in the pavilion, with Zhi put in overall charge.
translations.idiomatic: When the Secret Archives were built, he was made concurrent Director of the Secretariat, books from the Three Institutes were chosen for the new pavilion, and Zhi was placed in overall charge.

sentences.zh: 至每與李昉、王化基等觀書閣下，上必遣使賜宴，且命三館學士皆與焉。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhi viewed books in the pavilion with Li Fang, Wang Huaji, and others, the emperor would invariably send envoys to grant banquets, and also ordered all Hanlin academicians to attend.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhi joined Li Fang, Wang Huaji, and others to examine books in the pavilion, the emperor would send attendants with a feast, and ordered all Hanlin academicians to take part.

sentences.zh: 至是昇秘閣，次於三館，從至請也。

translations.literal: At this time the Elevated Secret Archives was ranked after the Three Institutes, following Zhi's request.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Elevated Secret Archives was ranked just below the Three Institutes, as Zhi had requested.

sentences.zh: 上嘗臨幸秘閣，出草書《千字文》為賜，至勒石，上曰：「《千文》乃梁武得破碑鍾繇書，命周興嗣次韻而成，理無足取。

translations.literal: The emperor once visited the Secret Archives in person, produced a cursive copy of the "Thousand-Character Classic" as a gift, and Zhi had it carved in stone. The emperor said, "The Thousand-Character Classic was composed when Emperor Wu of Liang obtained a broken stele of Zhong You's calligraphy and ordered Zhou Xingsi to arrange rhymes—it has little rational worth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once visited the Secret Archives in person and presented a cursive copy of the Thousand-Character Classic as a gift; Zhi had it carved on stone. The emperor said, "The Thousand-Character Classic was made when Emperor Wu of Liang obtained a broken stele of Zhong You's calligraphy and had Zhou Xingsi arrange rhymes—it has little worth as doctrine.

sentences.zh: 若有資於教化，莫《孝經》若也。」

translations.literal: If there is something that aids in transformation through teaching, nothing equals the Classic of Filial Piety."
translations.idiomatic: If a text is to serve moral instruction, nothing surpasses the Classic of Filial Piety."

sentences.zh: 乃書以賜至。

translations.literal: He thereupon wrote it out and bestowed it upon Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote out the Classic of Filial Piety and granted it to Zhi.

sentences.zh: 薦潘慎修、舒雅、杜鎬、吳淑等入充直館校理。

translations.literal: He recommended Pan Shenxiu, Shu Ya, Du Hao, and Wu Shu to serve as duty academicians and collators in the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Pan Shenxiu, Shu Ya, Du Hao, and Wu Shu to serve as duty editors and collators in the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 請購亡書，間以新書奏御，必便坐延見，恩禮甚厚。

translations.literal: He requested purchase of lost books; occasionally presenting new books to the throne, he was invariably granted audience at the informal seat with thick kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that lost books be purchased, and from time to time presented newly acquired volumes to the throne. The emperor invariably received him at the informal seat with exceptional kindness.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年，兼判國子監。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunhua he was made concurrent Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chunhua he was made concurrent Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 至上言：「《五經》書疏已板行，惟二《傳》、二《禮》、《孝經》、《論語》、《爾雅》七經疏未備，豈副仁君垂訓之意。

translations.literal: Zhi submitted a memorial: "The commentaries on the Five Classics have already been printed, but the commentaries on the two Traditions, the two Rites, the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, and the Erya—the seven classics—are not yet complete. How can this match the benevolent ruler's intent to extend instruction?
translations.idiomatic: Zhi submitted a memorial saying, "Commentaries on the Five Classics have already been printed, but those on the two Traditions, the two Rites, the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, and the Erya—the seven classics—are still incomplete. How can this satisfy Your Majesty's wish to spread learning?

sentences.zh: 今直講崔頤正、孫奭、崔偓佺皆勵精強學，博通經義，望令重加讎校，以備刊刻。」

translations.literal: The duty lecturers Cui Yizheng, Sun Shi, and Cui Weiquan all refine their studies and are broadly versed in the classics. I beg that they be ordered to collate them again in preparation for printing."
translations.idiomatic: The duty lecturers Cui Yizheng, Sun Shi, and Cui Weiquan are all diligent scholars thoroughly versed in the classics. I ask that they be ordered to collate these texts again so they may be printed."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 後又引吳淑、舒雅、杜鎬檢正訛謬，至與李沆總領而裁處之。

translations.literal: Later Wu Shu, Shu Ya, and Du Hao were again brought in to correct errors; Zhi and Li Hang took overall charge and made final decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wu Shu, Shu Ya, and Du Hao were again called in to correct errors, while Zhi and Li Hang supervised and made the final decisions.

sentences.zh: 至道初，真宗初正儲位，以至與李沆並兼賓客，詔太子事以師傅禮，真宗每見必先拜，至等上表，不敢當禮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhidao era, when Zhenzong was first established as heir apparent, Zhi and Li Hang were jointly made his guests. An edict ordered that matters of the heir apparent be treated with the etiquette due a teacher; whenever Zhenzong saw them he would first bow. Zhi and the others submitted memorials saying they dared not accept such rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhidao era, when Zhenzong was first established as heir apparent, Zhi and Li Hang were jointly appointed his tutors. An edict directed that the heir's affairs be conducted with the etiquette due teachers, and whenever Zhenzong saw them he bowed first. Zhi and the others submitted memorials saying they could not accept such honor.

sentences.zh: 詔答曰：「朕旁稽古訓，肇建承華，用選端良，資於輔導。

translations.literal: The edict in reply said: "We have examined ancient instruction and established the heir's establishment, selecting upright and good men to assist in guidance.
translations.idiomatic: The edict in reply said, "We have examined ancient instruction and established the heir's household, choosing upright and worthy men to assist in guidance.

sentences.zh: 借卿宿望，委以護調，蓋將勖以謙冲，故乃異其禮數。

translations.literal: Relying on your long-standing reputation, We entrust adjustment and protection; it is because We wish to encourage humility that We alter the ritual forms.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on your long-standing reputation, We entrust you with his training and protection. It is because We wish to encourage humility that We alter the ritual forms.

sentences.zh: 勿飾當仁之讓，副予知子之心。」

translations.literal: Do not adorn yourselves with the yielding of one who declines what is rightfully his; fulfill Our heart in knowing Our son."
translations.idiomatic: Do not embellish the modest refusal of one who ought to accept duty; fulfill Our trust in Our son."

sentences.zh: 至等相率謝。

translations.literal: Zhi and the others together expressed thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and the others together submitted their thanks.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂曰：「太子賢明仁孝，國本固矣。

translations.literal: Taizong said to them: "The heir apparent is worthy, humane, and filial; the foundation of the state is already secure.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said to them, "The heir apparent is worthy, humane, and filial; the foundation of the state is already secure.

sentences.zh: 卿等可盡心規誨，若動皆由禮，則宜贊助，事有未當，必須力言。

translations.literal: You may all wholeheartedly instruct and admonish him. If his actions accord with ritual, then you should support them; if anything is not fitting, you must speak out forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: You should all instruct and admonish him with your whole hearts. When his conduct accords with ritual, support it; when anything is amiss, speak out forcefully.

sentences.zh: 至於《禮》、《樂》、《詩》、《書》義有可裨益者，皆卿等素習，不假朕之言諭也。」

translations.literal: As for the meanings of the Rites, Music, Poetry, and Documents that may benefit him, these are what you have long studied—you need not wait for Our spoken instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Whatever in the Rites, Music, Poetry, and Documents may benefit him, you have long studied these yourselves and need not wait for Us to tell you."

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，拜工部尚書、參知政事。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded, Zhi was appointed Minister of Works and Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong took the throne, Zhi was appointed Minister of Works and Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 一日，上訪以靈武事，至上疏曰：「河湟之地，夷夏雜居，是以先王置之度外。

translations.literal: One day the emperor inquired about affairs at Lingwu. Zhi submitted a memorial saying: "The lands of the He and Huang are mixed with Yi and Xia; therefore the former kings placed them outside their concern.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor asked his view on affairs at Lingwu. Zhi submitted a memorial saying, "The lands of the He and Huang rivers are a mix of barbarian and Chinese peoples; the former kings therefore set them outside their direct rule.

sentences.zh: 繼遷異類，騷動疆埸，然臍不足弭其患，擢髮不足數其罪。

translations.literal: Jiqian is of another race; he troubles the borderlands, yet cutting off his navel would not end the trouble, nor would plucking out every hair enumerate his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqian is a foreign chieftain who troubles the frontier, yet killing him would not end the trouble, nor could one count all his offenses.

sentences.zh: 然聖人之道，務屈己含垢以安億民，蓋所損者小，所益者大。

translations.literal: Yet the way of the sage is to humble oneself and bear disgrace in order to secure peace for the people—the loss is small, the gain is great.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the way of the sage is to humble oneself and bear insult so as to secure peace for the people. What is lost is small; what is gained is great.

sentences.zh: 望陛下以元元為念，不以巨憝介意。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty, with the common people in mind, will not take this great villain to heart.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will keep the common people in view and not let this great enemy trouble your mind.

sentences.zh: 料彼脅從亦厭兵久矣，苟朝廷舍之不問，啖以厚利，縻以重爵，亦安肯迷而不復，訖於淪胥哉？

translations.literal: I expect that those coerced to follow him are also weary of war by now. If the court overlooks their offenses, feeds them with rich profit, and binds them with lofty ranks, how would they still be willing to go astray without return until they are utterly ruined?
translations.idiomatic: Those who followed him under coercion must be weary of war by now as well. If the court would overlook their offenses, entice them with rich rewards, and bind them with high rank, why would they persist in rebellion until they were utterly destroyed?

sentences.zh: 昨鄭文寶絕青鹽，使不入漢界，禁粒食使不及羌夷，致彼有詞，而我無謂，此之失策，雖悔何追。

translations.literal: Yesterday Zheng Wenbao cut off green salt so that it would not enter Han territory and barred grain provisions from reaching the Qiang and Yi, causing them to have complaint while we had no justification. This lost policy—even with regret, what can be pursued?
translations.idiomatic: Recently Zheng Wenbao cut off trade in green salt so it would not enter our territory and barred grain from reaching the Qiang and tribal peoples, giving them grievance while we had no grounds for complaint. That mistaken policy cannot be undone even with regret.

sentences.zh: 今若復禁止不許通糧，恐非制敵懷遠、不戰屈人之意。

translations.literal: Now if we again forbid the passage of grain, I fear this is not the intent of controlling enemies and cherishing the distant—of subduing others without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: To forbid grain shipments again would, I fear, run counter to the principle of winning over distant peoples and subduing foes without fighting.

sentences.zh: 昔唐代宗雖罪田承嗣而不禁魏鹽，陛下宜行此事，以安邊鄙。

translations.literal: In former times, though Tang Emperor Daizong punished Tian Chengsi, he did not forbid Wei salt. Your Majesty should carry out this matter to secure the border regions.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang times, although Emperor Daizong punished Tian Chengsi, he did not cut off salt from Wei. Your Majesty should do the same to secure the frontier.

sentences.zh: 使其族類有無交易，售鹽以利之，通糧以濟之，彼雖遠夷，必然向化，互相誥諭。

translations.literal: Let their clans trade in what they lack, sell salt to benefit them and pass grain to relieve them—even though they are distant barbarians, they will surely turn toward civilization and admonish one another.
translations.idiomatic: Let their tribes trade for what they lack, sell them salt for their profit and send grain to relieve their want. Though they are distant tribes, they will surely incline toward the court and counsel one another accordingly.

sentences.zh: 一旦懷恩，舍逆效順，則繼遷豎子孤而無輔，又安能為我蜂蠆哉！

translations.literal: Once they cherish grace, abandon rebellion and turn loyal, then Jiqian the junior lad will stand alone without support—how again could he be a hornet or scorpion for us!
translations.idiomatic: Once they accept favor and turn from rebellion to loyalty, Jiqian will be isolated and without allies. How then could he still sting us like hornets and scorpions?

sentences.zh: 今靈州不可不棄，非獨臣愚以為當然，若移朔方軍額於環州，亦一時之權也。

translations.literal: Now Lingzhou must be abandoned—not only does this foolish minister think it proper; to shift the Shuofang army designation to Huanzhou would also be a measure of the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhou cannot be held, in my view—not mine alone, but plainly so for all. Moving the Shuofang army headquarters to Huanzhou would be a timely expedient.

sentences.zh: 或指靈州為咽喉之地，西北要衝，安可棄之以為敵有，此不智之甚，非臣之所敢知也。」

translations.literal: Some call Lingzhou the throat of the land and a vital pass of the northwest—how can it be abandoned to become the enemy's possession? This is the height of folly, not what your humble servant dares understand."
translations.idiomatic: Some say Lingzhou is the throat of the northwest and a vital pass that must not be abandoned to the enemy. That is supreme folly, and not a view this minister can share."

sentences.zh: 後靈武卒不能守。

translations.literal: Later, Lingwu in the end could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, Lingwu could not be defended.

sentences.zh: 咸平元年，以目疾求解政柄，授武信軍節度，入辭節制，不允。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianping, citing eye disease he sought release from political power; he was given military command of Wuxin circuit and entered court to resign control—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianping, citing eye disease he asked to relinquish office. He was made military commissioner of Wuxin circuit and came to court to decline full control of the command, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 居二年，徙知河南府。

translations.literal: After two years he was transferred to administer Henan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was transferred to serve as prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 四年，以病求歸本鎮，許之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on grounds of illness he asked to return to his original command—permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, on grounds of illness he asked to return to his original post, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 詔甫下，卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: The edict had barely been issued when he died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: The edict had scarcely been issued when he died, at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中，詔給其子惟良、惟允、惟熙等奉終制。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Palace Attendant; an edict granted his sons Weiliang, Weiyun, Weixi, and others the mourning observances due at the end of service.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant, and an edict granted his sons Weiliang, Weiyun, Weixi, and the others the full mourning observances due at the end of service.

sentences.zh: 至嘗師徐鉉，手寫鉉及其弟鍇集，置於幾案。

translations.literal: Zhi had studied under Xu Xuan and copied by hand the collected works of Xuan and his brother Kai, placing them on his desk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had studied under Xu Xuan and copied by hand the collected works of Xuan and his brother Kai, which he kept on his desk.

sentences.zh: 又賦《五君詠》，為鉉及李昉、石熙載、王祐、李穆作也。

translations.literal: He also composed the Five Lords' Odes for Xu Xuan, Li Fang, Shi Xizai, Wang You, and Li Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the Five Lords' Odes in honor of Xu Xuan, Li Fang, Shi Xizai, Wang You, and Li Mu.

sentences.zh: 至剛嚴簡重，人士罕登其門。

translations.literal: Zhi was stern, concise, and weighty; men of standing rarely crossed his threshold.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was stern, reserved, and weighty in manner, and men of standing rarely called at his door.

sentences.zh: 性吝嗇。

translations.literal: By nature he was stingy.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was miserly.

sentences.zh: 幼育於知審，及貴，即逐其養子以利其資。

translations.literal: As a child he had been raised by Zhi Shen; once honored, he drove out Shen's adopted son to take that son's property.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he had been raised by Zhi Shen, but once he rose to high rank he drove out Shen's adopted son to seize that son's property.

sentences.zh: 知審因至亦至右金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Because of Zhi, Zhi Shen also rose to become Grand General of the Right Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Through Zhi's influence, Zhi Shen also rose to Grand General of the Right Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 辛仲甫

translations.literal: Xin Zhongfu
translations.idiomatic: Xin Zhongfu

sentences.zh: 辛仲甫，字之翰，汾州孝義人。

translations.literal: Xin Zhongfu, styled Zhihan, was a man of Xiaoyi in Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Zhongfu, styled Zhihan, was a native of Xiaoyi in Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖實，石州推官。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shi was investigating officer of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shi served as investigating officer of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖迪，壽陽令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Di was magistrate of Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Di was magistrate of Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 父藩，河東節度判官。

translations.literal: His father Fan was administrative aide of the Hedong military commission.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fan served as administrative aide to the Hedong military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 仲甫少好學，及長，能吏事，偉姿儀，器局沉厚。

translations.literal: Zhongfu from youth loved learning; when grown he was capable in official affairs, of imposing bearing, and of a disposition deep and weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu loved learning from youth, and when grown he proved capable in administration, with imposing bearing and a deep, steady temperament.

sentences.zh: 周廣順中，郭崇掌親軍，領武定節制，置仲甫掌書記。

translations.literal: In the Guangshun era of Zhou, Guo Chong commanded the imperial guard and held the Wuding military commission, appointing Zhongfu as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangshun era of Later Zhou, Guo Chong commanded the imperial guard and held the Wuding commission, and appointed Zhongfu chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，出鎮澶淵，仍署舊職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he went out to command at Chanyuan and still held him in his former post.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiande he went out to command at Chanyuan and kept Zhongfu in the same post.

sentences.zh: 崇所親吏為廂虞候，部民有被劫殺者，訴陰識賊魁，即捕盜吏也，官不敢詰。

translations.literal: A favorite officer of Chong's served as garrison commander. When a subject of the commandery was robbed and killed, the complaint secretly identified the bandit chief as the very officer who caught thieves, and the officials dared not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: One of Chong's favorite officers served as garrison commander. When a local resident was robbed and murdered, the complaint secretly identified the bandit leader as that very officer charged with catching thieves, and the officials dared not pursue the case.

sentences.zh: 仲甫請自捕逮，鞫之，吏故稽其獄，仲甫曰：「民被寇害而使自誣服，蠹政甚矣，焉用僚佐為？」

translations.literal: Zhongfu asked to capture and try the case himself. The officer deliberately delayed the trial. Zhongfu said: "The people suffer bandit harm yet are made to confess falsely—how greatly government is corrupted! Of what use are assistants?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu asked to make the arrest and conduct the trial himself. The officer deliberately delayed the case. Zhongfu said, "The people suffer robbery and murder, yet are made to confess falsely—how corrupt is government! What use are assistants?"

sentences.zh: 請易吏以雪冤憤。

translations.literal: He asked to replace the officer to clear the injustice and anger.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the officer be replaced to clear the injustice and public anger.

sentences.zh: 崇悟，移鞫之，乃得實狀。

translations.literal: Chong understood, transferred the trial, and thus obtained the true facts.
translations.idiomatic: Chong took his meaning, transferred the case for retrial, and thus obtained the true facts.

sentences.zh: 崇移鎮真定，改深、趙、鎮觀察判官。

translations.literal: When Chong was transferred to command at Zhending, Zhongfu was changed to administrative aide of the Shen, Zhao, and Zhen observation commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong was transferred to command at Zhending, Zhongfu became administrative aide of the Shen, Zhao, and Zhen observation commission.

sentences.zh: 太祖受命，以崇為監軍。

translations.literal: When Taizu received the Mandate, Chong was made army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu received the Mandate, Chong was appointed army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 陳思誨密奏崇有奸狀，上怒且疑，遣中使馳往驗之。

translations.literal: Chen Sihui secretly memorialized that Chong had treacherous conduct. The emperor was angry and suspicious and sent a palace envoy posthaste to verify it.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sihui secretly reported that Chong had engaged in treacherous conduct. The emperor grew angry and suspicious and sent a palace envoy posthaste to investigate.

sentences.zh: 未至，崇憂懣失據，謂賓佐曰：「苟人主不察，為之奈何？」

translations.literal: Before the envoy arrived, Chong was anxious and distraught and said to his staff: "If the sovereign does not discern the truth, what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Before the envoy arrived, Chong was anxious and at a loss. He said to his staff, "If the sovereign does not see the truth, what can we do?"

sentences.zh: 皆愕相視。

translations.literal: All stared at one another in dismay.
translations.idiomatic: All stared at one another in dismay.

sentences.zh: 仲甫曰：「皇帝膺運，公首效節，軍民處置，率循常度，且何以加辭。

translations.literal: Zhongfu said: "The emperor has received the Mandate; you were the first to show loyalty. In disposing army and people you have all followed the usual rules—what more can be said against you?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu said, "The emperor has received the Mandate, and you were the first to show loyalty. In managing army and people you have followed established practice throughout—what case can be made against you?

sentences.zh: 第遠偵使者，率僚屬盡郊迎禮，聽彼伺察，久當自辨矣。」

translations.literal: Only send scouts far out to watch for the envoy, lead all subordinates in full suburban welcome rites, and let him observe—before long he will clear himself."
translations.idiomatic: Only send scouts far ahead to watch for the envoy, lead all your subordinates in the full suburban welcome ceremony, and let him observe you. In time the truth will clear itself."

sentences.zh: 崇如其言。

translations.literal: Chong did as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Chong followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 使者至，視崇無他意，還奏，上大喜，歸罪於思誨。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived and saw that Chong had no other intent, he returned and reported. The emperor was greatly pleased and laid the blame on Sihui.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy arrived and saw that Chong had no ulterior intent, he returned and reported. The emperor was greatly pleased and blamed Sihui instead.

sentences.zh: 仲甫又隨崇為平盧軍節度判官。

translations.literal: Zhongfu again followed Chong as administrative aide of the Pinglu military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu again followed Chong as administrative aide of the Pinglu military commission.

sentences.zh: 崇卒，改鄆、齊觀察判官，累雪冤枉。

translations.literal: When Chong died, he was changed to administrative aide of the Yan and Qi observation commission and repeatedly cleared wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: After Chong died, he became administrative aide of the Yan and Qi observation commission and repeatedly cleared wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 乾德五年，入拜右補闕，出知光州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiande he entered court as Right Supplementation Censor and went out to administer Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qiande he was appointed Right Supplementation Censor and sent out to serve as prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 州有橫河與城直，會霖潦暴疾，水溢潰廬舍。

translations.literal: The prefecture had a cross-river aligned with the city wall. When heavy rains and sudden floods came, the water overflowed and destroyed houses.
translations.idiomatic: A river ran across the prefecture in line with the city wall. When torrential rains and sudden flooding came, the waters overflowed and destroyed dwellings.

sentences.zh: 仲甫集船數百艘，軍資民儲，皆賴以濟。

translations.literal: Zhongfu gathered several hundred boats; military supplies and civilian stores all relied on this to be saved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu gathered several hundred boats, and both military supplies and civilian stores were saved by this means.

sentences.zh: 六年，移知彭州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to administer Pengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to serve as prefect of Pengzhou.

sentences.zh: 州卒誘營兵及諸屯戍，謀以長春節宴集日為亂。

translations.literal: Soldiers of the prefecture incited camp troops and various garrison posts to plot rebellion on the day of the Changchun festival gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural soldiers incited camp troops and various garrison posts to plot a rising on the day of the Changchun festival banquet.

sentences.zh: 屬春初，仲甫出城巡視，見壕中草深，意可藏伏，命燒薙之。

translations.literal: It being early spring, Zhongfu went out of the city on inspection, saw the grass in the moat was deep and thought it could hide ambushers, and ordered it burned and cut down.
translations.idiomatic: Early that spring Zhongfu went outside the city on inspection, saw the moat grass grown deep and fit to conceal ambushers, and ordered it burned and cleared.

sentences.zh: 凶黨疑謀泄，有自首者，擒百餘人，盡斬之。

translations.literal: The conspirators suspected the plot had leaked; some turned themselves in. More than a hundred were seized and all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The conspirators suspected the plot had leaked, and some turned themselves in. More than a hundred were seized and all beheaded.

sentences.zh: 先是州少種樹，暑無所休，仲甫課民栽柳蔭行路，郡人德之，名為『補闕柳』。

translations.literal: Previously the prefecture had few planted trees and in summer there was nowhere to rest from the heat. Zhongfu ordered the people to plant willows to shade the roads. The people of the commandery were grateful and called them the "Supplementation Censor Willows."
translations.idiomatic: Previously the prefecture had few trees, and in summer travelers had no shade. Zhongfu ordered the people to plant willows along the roads. The people were grateful and called them the "Supplementation Censor Willows."

sentences.zh: 太祖問群臣文武兼資者為誰，趙普以仲甫對。

translations.literal: Taizu asked his ministers who combined civil and military ability; Zhao Pu named Zhongfu.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu asked his ministers who combined civil and military talent, and Zhao Pu named Zhongfu.

sentences.zh: 徙益州兵馬都監，代還，選為三司戶部判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be military supervisor of Yizhou; when his replacement returned, he was selected as administrative judge of the Revenue Section of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military supervisor of Yizhou, and on his return was selected administrative judge of the Revenue Section of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，遷起居舍人，奉使契丹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent and sent on embassy to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent and sent on embassy to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 遼主問：「党進何如人？

translations.literal: The Liao ruler asked: "What sort of man is Dang Jin?
translations.idiomatic: The Liao ruler asked, "What sort of man is Dang Jin?

sentences.zh: 如進之比有幾？」

translations.literal: How many are there like Jin?"
translations.idiomatic: How many men like him are there?"

sentences.zh: 仲甫曰：「國家名將輩出，如進鷹犬材耳，何足道哉！」

translations.literal: Zhongfu said: "Our state's famous generals come forth in succession; someone like Jin is merely hawk-and-dog material—how is he worth speaking of!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu said, "Famous generals of our state come forth in succession. A man like Jin is merely hawk-and-hound stuff—how is he worth mentioning!"

sentences.zh: 遼主欲留之，仲甫曰：「信以成命，義不可留，有死而已。」

translations.literal: The Liao ruler wished to detain him. Zhongfu said: "Faith completes the mandate; by righteousness one cannot stay—there is only death."
translations.idiomatic: The Liao ruler wished to detain him. Zhongfu said, "Faith fulfills the charge; by duty one cannot stay—only death awaits."

sentences.zh: 遼主竟不能屈。

translations.literal: In the end the Liao ruler could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the Liao ruler could not bend him.

sentences.zh: 使還，以刑部郎中知成都府。

translations.literal: On his return from the embassy he was made Bureau Vice Director of Punishments and prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: On his return from the embassy he was made Bureau Vice Director of Punishments and appointed prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 既至，奏免歲輸銅錢，罷榷酤，政尚寬簡，蜀人安之。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he memorialized to exempt the annual delivery of copper cash and abolished the liquor monopoly. His government favored lenience and simplicity, and the people of Shu were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, he memorialized to end the annual delivery of copper cash and abolished the liquor monopoly. His administration favored lenience and simplicity, and the people of Shu were reassured.

sentences.zh: 八年，加右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was given the additional title of Right Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was given the additional title of Right Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 時彭州盜賊連結為害，詔捕未獲。

translations.literal: At that time bandits in Pengzhou were linked in harm; an edict ordered their capture but they were not taken.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits in Pengzhou were acting in concert, and though an edict ordered their capture, none were taken.

sentences.zh: 仲甫誘令自縛詣吏者凡百餘人，餘因散去。

translations.literal: Zhongfu induced more than a hundred to bind themselves and come to the officials; the rest therefore dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu induced more than a hundred to bind themselves and surrender to the authorities, and the rest dispersed.

sentences.zh: 九年，入知開封府，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he entered to govern Kaifeng prefecture and was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he entered to govern Kaifeng prefecture and was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，拜給事中、參知政事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he was made Attendant Gentleman and Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi he was made Attendant Gentleman and Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 端拱中，進戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: During the Duangong era he was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: During the Duangong era he was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時呂蒙正以長厚居相位，王沔任事，仲甫從容其間而已。

translations.literal: At that time Lü Mengzheng, generous and steady, held the chief ministership while Wang Mian handled affairs; Zhongfu kept his composure between them, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lü Mengzheng, generous and steady, held the chief ministership while Wang Mian handled affairs; Zhongfu kept his composure between them, that was all.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，以足疾罷為工部尚書，出知陳州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, because of foot ailment he was removed as Minister of Works and sent out to govern Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua, because of foot ailment he was removed as Minister of Works and sent out to govern Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 代歸，會蜀有寇，以仲甫素著恩信，將令輿疾招撫，以疾未行。

translations.literal: When his replacement returned, bandits arose in Shu. Because Zhongfu was known for kindness and trustworthiness, he was to be ordered to pacify them despite illness, but illness prevented him from going.
translations.idiomatic: When his replacement returned, bandits arose in Shu. Because Zhongfu was known for kindness and trustworthiness, he was to be ordered to pacify them despite illness, but illness prevented him from going.

sentences.zh: 無何，以太子少保致仕。

translations.literal: Before long he retired as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he retired as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，加太子少傅。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong took the throne, he was given the additional title of Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong took the throne, he was given the additional title of Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，卒，年七十四，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping he died, aged seventy-four, and was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping he died, aged seventy-four, and was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 子若冲、若虛、若蒙、若濟、若渝，皆能其官。

translations.literal: His sons Ruochong, Ruoxu, Ruomeng, Ruoji, and Ruoyu all proved capable in their offices.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Ruochong, Ruoxu, Ruomeng, Ruoji, and Ruoyu all proved capable in their offices.

sentences.zh: 孫有孚、有隣，俱中進士。

translations.literal: His grandsons Youfu and Youlin both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His grandsons Youfu and Youlin both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，宰相趙普出守西洛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua, Grand Councilor Zhao Pu went out to guard the Western Luo.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chunhua, Grand Councilor Zhao Pu was sent out to guard the Western Luo capital.

sentences.zh: 呂蒙正以寬簡自任，政事多決於沔，沔與張齊賢同掌樞務，頗不叶。

translations.literal: Lü Mengzheng took lenience and simplicity as his charge; most government affairs were decided by Mian. Mian and Zhang Qixian jointly held key affairs and were rather at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Mengzheng took lenience and simplicity as his guiding principle, but most government affairs were decided by Mian. Mian and Zhang Qixian jointly held key affairs and were often at odds.

sentences.zh: 齊賢出知代州，沔遂為副使，參預政事。

translations.literal: Qixian went out to administer Daizhou; Mian then became deputy commissioner and took part in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Qixian was sent out to administer Daizhou, Mian became deputy commissioner and took part in government affairs.

sentences.zh: 陳恕好苛察，亦嘗與沔忤。

translations.literal: Chen Shu favored harsh scrutiny and had also clashed with Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shu favored harsh scrutiny and had also clashed with Mian.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，齊賢洎恕參知政事，沔不自安，慮僚屬有以中書舊事告齊賢等，會左司諫王禹偁上言：「自今宰相及樞密使不得於本廳見客，許於都堂延接。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, Qixian and Shu became Vice Grand Councilors. Mian was ill at ease, fearing that subordinates might report old affairs of the Secretariat to Qixian and the others. It happened that Left Remonstrator Wang Yucheng submitted a memorial saying: "From now on grand councilors and commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs may not receive guests in their own offices; they are permitted to receive them in the main hall."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua, Qixian and Shu became Vice Grand Councilors. Mian grew uneasy, fearing that subordinates might report old Secretariat affairs to Qixian and the others. At that time Left Remonstrator Wang Yucheng submitted a memorial saying, "From now on grand councilors and commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs may not receive guests in their own offices, but only in the main hall of the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 沔喜，即奏行之。

translations.literal: Mian was pleased and immediately memorialized to put it into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was pleased and immediately memorialized to put the proposal into effect.

sentences.zh: 直史館謝泌以為如此是疑大臣以私也，疏駁之。

translations.literal: Academician of the Historiography Institute Xie Bi held that this was to suspect grand ministers of private dealings and submitted a memorial refuting it.
translations.idiomatic: Academician of the Historiography Institute Xie Bi held that this amounted to suspecting grand ministers of private dealings and submitted a memorial refuting it.

sentences.zh: 太宗追還前詔，沔暨恕因是罷守本官。

translations.literal: Taizong recalled the previous edict; Mian and Shu therefore resigned and kept only their original offices.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong recalled the previous edict, and Mian and Shu therefore left office and retained only their original ranks.

sentences.zh: 翌日，蒙正亦罷。

translations.literal: The next day Mengzheng was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Mengzheng was dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 沔見上，涕泣，不願離左右。

translations.literal: When Mian saw the emperor he wept and said he did not wish to leave his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Mian saw the emperor he wept and said he did not wish to leave his side.

sentences.zh: 未幾，鬚鬢皆白。

translations.literal: Before long his beard and temples were all white.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his beard and temples had turned completely white.

sentences.zh: 會省吏事發，連中書，因有奏毀者。

translations.literal: It happened that an affair of a provincial clerk broke out, implicating the Secretariat, and there were memorials slandering them.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that a provincial clerk's misconduct came to light, implicating the Secretariat, and some submitted memorials attacking them.

sentences.zh: 上語毀者曰：「呂蒙正有大臣體，王沔甚明敏。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to the slanderers: "Lü Mengzheng has the bearing of a great minister; Wang Mian is very clear and keen."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to the attackers, "Lü Mengzheng has the bearing of a great minister, and Wang Mian is very clear and keen."

sentences.zh: 毀者慚而止。

translations.literal: The slanderers were ashamed and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The attackers were ashamed and desisted.

sentences.zh: 三年，上欲黜陟官吏，命沔與謝泌、王仲華同知京朝官考課。

translations.literal: In the third year the emperor wished to promote and demote officials and ordered Mian, together with Xie Bi and Wang Zhonghua, jointly to oversee the performance review of capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the emperor wished to promote and demote officials and ordered Mian, together with Xie Bi and Wang Zhonghua, jointly to oversee the performance review of capital officials.

sentences.zh: 沔上言，應京朝官殿犯，乞令刑部條報，以贓及公私罪分三等以聞。

translations.literal: Mian submitted a memorial saying that for capital officials guilty of serious offenses, he asked that the Ministry of Punishments report item by item, dividing bribery and public and private crimes into three grades for report.
translations.idiomatic: Mian submitted a memorial asking that for capital officials guilty of serious offenses, the Ministry of Punishments report in detail, dividing bribery and public and private crimes into three grades for the court's review.

sentences.zh: 立法苛察，欲因是以求再用。

translations.literal: He made law harsh and scrutinizing, wishing by this means to seek reuse in office.
translations.idiomatic: He framed the law in harsh and scrutinizing terms, hoping thereby to win reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 受命甫旬日，方視事，以暴疾卒，年四十三，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He had received the appointment only ten days before and had just begun to conduct affairs when he died suddenly of acute illness, aged forty-three. He was posthumously given the title of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He had held the appointment only ten days and had just begun to conduct affairs when he died suddenly of acute illness, at the age of forty-three. He was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 沔聰察敏辯，有適時之用，上前言事，能委曲敷繹。

translations.literal: Mian was perceptive, keen, and eloquent, with timely usefulness. Before the emperor in speaking of affairs he could unfold and explain matters with tact.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was perceptive, keen, and eloquent, with timely usefulness. When he spoke before the emperor he could unfold and explain matters with tact.

sentences.zh: 每對御讀所試進士辭賦，音吐明暢，經讀者多中高第。

translations.literal: Whenever he read before the emperor the rhapsodies of jinshi candidates under examination, his voice was clear and flowing; many who had been read by him won high ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he read before the emperor the examination essays of jinshi candidates, his delivery was clear and fluent, and many of those he read won high ranks.

sentences.zh: 性苛刻，少誠信。

translations.literal: By nature he was harsh and demanding, with little trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was harsh and demanding, and little trustworthy.

sentences.zh: 掌機務日，凡謁見者必啖以甘言，皆喜過望，既而進退非允，人胥怨之。

translations.literal: On the days he held key affairs, every visitor was sure to be fed sweet words; all rejoiced beyond expectation, yet afterward promotions and demotions were not as promised, and everyone resented him.
translations.idiomatic: While he held key affairs, every visitor was greeted with flattering words, and all rejoiced beyond expectation. Yet when promotions and demotions did not follow as promised, everyone resented him.

sentences.zh: 沔弟淮，太平興國五年進士，任殿中丞。

translations.literal: Mian's younger brother Huai, a jinshi of the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, served as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Mian's younger brother Huai, a jinshi of the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, served as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 嘗掌香藥榷易院，坐贓論當棄市，以沔故，詔杖一百，降定遠主簿。

translations.literal: He once directed the Fragrant Medicines Monopoly Exchange Office and on a bribery conviction was sentenced to execution in the marketplace. Because of Mian, an edict ordered one hundred strokes of the staff and demotion to Registrar of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He once directed the Fragrant Medicines Monopoly Exchange Office and, on a bribery conviction, was sentenced to death. Because of Mian, an edict ordered one hundred strokes of the staff and demotion to registrar of Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 沔以是頻為寇準所詆云。

translations.literal: Because of this Mian was frequently slandered by Kou Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason Mian was frequently attacked by Kou Zhun.

sentences.zh: 溫仲舒

translations.literal: Wen Zhongshu
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhongshu

sentences.zh: 溫仲舒，字秉陽，河南人。

translations.literal: Wen Zhongshu, styled Bingyang, was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhongshu, styled Bingyang, was a native of Henan.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，舉進士，為大理評事，通判吉州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination, became Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review, and served as deputy prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination, became Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review, and served as deputy prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 再遷秘書丞、知汾州，坐事除名。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Secretary of the Secretariat and prefect of Fenzhou, but on an offense was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Secretary of the Secretariat and prefect of Fenzhou, but on an offense was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復起為右讚善大夫，通判睦州。

translations.literal: Before long he was restored as Right Supporter of Goodness Grandee and deputy prefect of Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored as Right Supporter of Goodness Grandee and deputy prefect of Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，拜右正言、直史館、判戶部憑由司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was appointed Right Rectifier, academician of the Historiography Institute, and administrator of the Revenue Section's Credentials Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Duangong he was appointed Right Rectifier, academician of the Historiography Institute, and administrator of the Revenue Section's Credentials Office.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜工部郎中、樞密直學士，知三班院。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Bureau Director of Works, direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and director of the Three-Rank Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed Bureau Director of Works, direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and director of the Three-Rank Office.

sentences.zh: 秋，彗星見，召對別殿，仲舒以為「國家平太原以來，燕、代之交，城守年深，殺傷剽掠，彼此迭見。

translations.literal: In autumn a comet appeared. He was summoned to audience in a separate hall. Zhongshu held that "since the state pacified Taiyuan, along the border of Yan and Dai, garrison defense has gone on for years, with killing, wounding, and plunder alternating between the two sides.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn a comet appeared. He was summoned to audience in a separate hall. Zhongshu said, "Since the state pacified Taiyuan, along the Yan and Dai frontier garrison defense has gone on for years, with killing, wounding, and plunder alternating between the two sides.

sentences.zh: 大河以北，農桑廢業，戶口減耗。

translations.literal: North of the Great River, farming and sericulture lie waste and households are diminished.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Yellow River, farming and sericulture lie in ruins and the population has declined.

sentences.zh: 凋弊之餘，極力奉邊。

translations.literal: On top of this exhaustion they strain every effort to supply the border.
translations.idiomatic: On top of this exhaustion they strain every effort to supply the frontier.

sentences.zh: 丁壯備徭，老弱供賦。

translations.literal: Able-bodied men stand ready for corvée; the old and weak supply taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Able-bodied men stand ready for corvée labor, while the old and weak supply taxes.

sentences.zh: 遺廬壞堵，不亡即死。

translations.literal: Abandoned huts and ruined walls—if they do not perish, they die.
translations.idiomatic: Abandoned homes and ruined walls—those who escape death still face ruin.

sentences.zh: 邪人媚上，猶云樂輸。

translations.literal: Vile men who curry favor with their superiors still say the people gladly submit levies.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked officials who flatter their superiors still claim the people pay taxes willingly.

sentences.zh: 加以兵卒踐更，行者辛苦，居者怨曠。

translations.literal: Moreover, with soldiers treading rotation duty, travelers suffer hardship and those who remain behind lament separation.
translations.idiomatic: On top of this, soldiers cycle through corvée rotations; those on the march endure hardship, while those left behind chafe at abandonment.

sentences.zh: 願推恩宥，以綏民庶。」

translations.literal: I beg that favor and pardon be extended to pacify the common people."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty extend grace and pardon to bring peace to the people."

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉納之，遂赦河北。

translations.literal: The Taizong emperor praised and accepted this, and thereupon pardoned Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong emperor praised and accepted his counsel, and thereupon granted an amnesty in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，拜右諫議大夫、樞密副使，改同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua he was appointed Right Remonstrance Councilor and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and was changed to Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua he was appointed Right Remonstrance Councilor and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then made Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年，罷知秦州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was dismissed and made prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was relieved of his central post and appointed prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，俗雜羌、戎，有兩馬家、朵藏、梟波等部，唐末以來，居於渭河之南，大洛、小洛門砦，多產良木，為其所據。

translations.literal: Previously, the region was mixed with Qiang and Rong peoples; there were the Liangma, Duocang, Xiaobo, and other tribes who, since the late Tang, had dwelt south of the Wei River at the Great Luo and Little Luomen stockades, which produced much fine timber that they held.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the region was intermixed with Qiang and Rong peoples. Tribes such as the Liangma, Duocang, and Xiaobo had lived south of the Wei River at the Great Luo and Little Luomen stockades since the late Tang. These places produced fine timber, which the tribes controlled.

sentences.zh: 歲調卒采伐給京師，必以貲假道於羌戶。

translations.literal: Each year conscript laborers were dispatched to fell timber for the capital, and had to pay tolls to pass through Qiang households.
translations.idiomatic: Each year conscript laborers were sent to harvest timber for the capital and had to pay passage fees to Qiang households along the route.

sentences.zh: 然不免攘奪，甚至殺掠，為平民患。

translations.literal: Yet they could not avoid plunder, and at times even killing and raiding, which plagued the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they still could not escape plunder, and at times even killing and raiding, which became a scourge to the common people.

sentences.zh: 仲舒至，部兵歷按諸砦，諭其酋以威信，諸部獻地內屬。

translations.literal: When Zhongshu arrived, he led troops on inspection through the stockades and instructed the chieftains with authority and good faith; the tribes presented land and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongshu arrived, he led troops on inspection through the stockades and won the chieftains over with authority and good faith; the tribes presented land and submitted to the court.

sentences.zh: 既而悉徙其部落於渭北，立堡砦以限之。

translations.literal: Thereafter he moved all their tribes north of the Wei and established fortified stockades to confine them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he moved all their tribes north of the Wei and established fortified stockades to keep them within bounds.

sentences.zh: 民感其惠，為畫像祠之。

translations.literal: The people were grateful for his kindness and painted his portrait for worship.
translations.idiomatic: The people were grateful for his kindness and painted his portrait for veneration.

sentences.zh: 會有言仲舒生事者，上謂近臣曰：「仲舒嘗總機密之職，在吾左右，當以綏懷為務。

translations.literal: When someone reported that Zhongshu was stirring up trouble, the emperor said to his close ministers, "Zhongshu once held a post governing state secrets and stood at my side; he ought to make soothing the people his task.
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported that Zhongshu was stirring up trouble, the emperor said to his close ministers, "Zhongshu once held the most confidential posts and stood at my side; his duty should be to win people over by kindness.

sentences.zh: 古伊、洛之間，尚有羌、渾雜居，況此羌部內屬，素居渭南，土著已久，一旦擅意斥逐，或至騷動，又煩吾關右之民。」

translations.literal: Between ancient Yi and Luo there were still Qiang and Hun living in mixture—how much more so these Qiang tribes who have submitted and long dwelt south of the Wei as natives. If he arbitrarily drives them out, there may be unrest, and again my people west of the Pass will be troubled."
translations.idiomatic: Even between ancient Yi and Luo, Qiang and Hun still lived intermingled—how much more so these Qiang tribes, now submitted, who have long been natives south of the Wei. If he drives them out on his own authority, there may be unrest, and again the people west of the Pass will suffer."

sentences.zh: 乃命知鳳翔薛惟吉與仲舒對易其任。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered Xue Weiji, prefect of Fengxiang, to exchange posts with Zhongshu.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon ordered Xue Weiji, prefect of Fengxiang, to exchange posts with Zhongshu.

sentences.zh: 連知興元、江陵二府，加給事中。

translations.literal: In succession he served as prefect of Xingyuan and Jiangling, and was promoted to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In succession he governed Xingyuan and Jiangling and was promoted to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 會內侍藍繼宗使秦州還，言得地甚利。

translations.literal: When the inner attendant Lan Jizong returned from an embassy to Qinzhou, he reported that the land taken was very profitable.
translations.idiomatic: When the inner attendant Lan Jizong returned from a mission to Qinzhou, he reported that the land secured there was highly profitable.

sentences.zh: 乃召仲舒，拜戶部侍郎，尋參知政事。

translations.literal: Zhongshu was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue, and soon after made Associate Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu was summoned, appointed Vice Minister of Revenue, and soon made Associate Administrator.

sentences.zh: 二砦後為內地，歲獲巨木之利。

translations.literal: The two stockades later became inner territory, and each year brought great profit in timber.
translations.idiomatic: The two stockades later became inner territory, yielding great annual profits in timber.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，拜禮部尚書，罷政，出知河陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was appointed Minister of Rites, left the administration, and went out as prefect of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianping he was appointed Minister of Rites, left the central administration, and went out as prefect of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 逾年，知開封府。

translations.literal: After more than a year he became prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was appointed prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 五年，以京府務劇求罷，遂以本官兼御史中丞，尋遷刑部尚書、知天雄軍，徙河南。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, because the capital prefecture's duties were heavy he sought dismissal; he was then given his present rank concurrently as Censor-in-Chief, and soon transferred to Minister of Justice and military commissioner of Tianxiong, then moved to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, because the capital prefecture's duties were onerous he sought dismissal; he was then given his present rank concurrently as Censor-in-Chief, and soon transferred to Minister of Justice and military commissioner of Tianxiong, then moved to Henan.

sentences.zh: 景德中，幷州缺守，上以北門重鎮須大臣鎮撫，非張齊賢、溫仲舒不可，令宰相諭旨，皆不願往。

translations.literal: During Jingde, Bingzhou lacked a defender; the emperor held that this northern gate stronghold required a great minister to pacify it, and that none but Zhang Qixian or Wen Zhongshu would do. He ordered the chief ministers to convey his intent, but both were unwilling to go.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingde, Bingzhou lacked a defender. The emperor held that this northern gate stronghold required a great minister to pacify it and that none but Zhang Qixian or Wen Zhongshu would do. He ordered the chief ministers to convey his intent, but both declined to go.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復知審官院。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made director of the Court of Review.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again made director of the Court of Review.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符中，進秩戶部尚書。

translations.literal: During Dazhong Xiangfu his rank was advanced to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: During Dazhong Xiangfu his rank was advanced to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 三年，判昭文館大學士，命下，卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall; when the order was issued, he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall; the order had barely been issued when he died, aged sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈左僕射，諡恭肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the post of Left Vice Director and the posthumous title Gongsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the post of Left Vice Director and the posthumous title Gongsu.

sentences.zh: 仲舒敏於應務。

translations.literal: Zhongshu was quick in handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu was quick-witted in practical affairs.

sentences.zh: 少與呂蒙正契厚，又同登第。

translations.literal: In youth he was close with Lü Mengzheng, and they passed the examinations together.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was on close terms with Lü Mengzheng, and they passed the examinations in the same year.

sentences.zh: 仲舒黜廢累年，蒙正居中書，極力援引，及被任用，反攻蒙正，士論薄之。

translations.literal: Zhongshu was demoted and idle for many years; Mengzheng, holding the Secretariat, exerted himself to recommend him. Once employed, he turned and attacked Mengzheng, and public opinion held him in low regard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu had been demoted and idle for many years; Mengzheng, holding the Secretariat, exerted himself to recommend him. Once in office, he turned and attacked Mengzheng, and opinion among the gentlemen held him in low regard.

sentences.zh: 自為正言至貳樞密，皆與寇準同進，時人謂之『溫寇』。

translations.literal: From Rectifier to second-rank Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs he advanced together with Kou Zhun; people of the time called them "Wen-Kou."
translations.idiomatic: From Right Rectifier to second-rank Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs he rose together with Kou Zhun; people of the time called them "Wen-Kou."

sentences.zh: 子嗣宗、嗣良、嗣先、嗣立。

translations.literal: His sons were Sizong, Siliang, Sixian, and Sili.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Sizong, Siliang, Sixian, and Sili.

sentences.zh: 仲舒既卒，帝憫其孤弱，並祿以官。

translations.literal: After Zhongshu died, the emperor pitied his orphaned weakness and granted salaries and offices to them all.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongshu died, the emperor pitied his orphaned sons and granted them all salaries and offices.

sentences.zh: 王化基

translations.literal: Wang Huaji
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huaji

sentences.zh: 王化基，字永圖，鎮定人。

translations.literal: Wang Huaji, styled Yongtu, was a man of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huaji, courtesy name Yongtu, was a native of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，舉進士，為大理評事，通判常州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination, became Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review, and served as deputy prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination, became Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review, and served as deputy prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷太子右贊善大夫、知嵐州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Supporter of Goodness Grandee and prefect of Lanzhou.
