translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Supporter of Goodness Grandee and prefect of Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時趙普為相，建議以驟用人無益於治，改淮南節度判官，入為著作郎，遷右拾遺，抗疏自薦。

translations.literal: At the time Zhao Pu was chief minister and proposed that sudden appointments were of no benefit to governance; Huaji was changed to military administration judge of Huainan, entered the capital as Compiler, was transferred to Right Remembrancer, and submitted a memorial recommending himself.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhao Pu was chief minister and argued that sudden appointments did the state no good. Huaji was reassigned as military administration judge of Huainan, entered the capital as Compiler, was made Right Remembrancer, and submitted a bold memorial recommending himself.

sentences.zh: 太宗覽奏曰：「化基自結人主，慷慨之士也。」

translations.literal: The Taizong emperor read the memorial and said, "Huaji has attached himself to the ruler on his own initiative—a man of generous spirit."
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong emperor read the memorial and said, "Huaji has sought the ruler's favor on his own initiative—a man of generous spirit."

sentences.zh: 召試，知制誥，以右諫議大夫權御史中丞。

translations.literal: He summoned him for examination, made him Drafter, and gave him the concurrent post of Right Remonstrance Councilor acting as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned him for examination, made him Drafter, and gave him the concurrent post of Right Remonstrance Councilor acting as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 一日，侍便殿，問以邊事，對曰：「治天下猶植木焉，所患根本未固，固則枝幹不足憂。

translations.literal: One day, attending in the informal hall, he was asked about frontier affairs and replied, "Governing the empire is like planting a tree: what one fears is that the root is not firm; once firm, the branches need not worry one.
translations.idiomatic: One day, while attending in the informal hall, he was asked about frontier affairs and replied, "Governing the empire is like planting a tree: what one fears is that the roots are not firm; once they are firm, the branches need cause no worry.

sentences.zh: 朝廷治，則邊鄙何患乎不安？」

translations.literal: If the court is well governed, what need is there to fear that the frontier will not be secure?
translations.idiomatic: When the court is well governed, why should one fear that the frontier will not be secure?"

sentences.zh: 又嘗令薦士，即一疏數十人，王嗣宗、薛映、耿望，皆其人也。

translations.literal: He was also once ordered to recommend scholars; in a single memorial he named several dozen men, among them Wang Sigong, Xue Ying, and Geng Wang.
translations.idiomatic: He was also once ordered to recommend scholars; in a single memorial he named several dozen men, among them Wang Sigong, Xue Ying, and Geng Wang.

sentences.zh: 化基嘗慕范滂為人，獻《澄清略》，言時事有五：

translations.literal: Huaji once admired Fan Pang as a man and presented the "Clarification Summary," setting forth five points on current affairs:
translations.idiomatic: Huaji once admired Fan Pang and presented the "Clarification Summary," setting forth five points on current affairs:

sentences.zh: 其一，復尚書省，曰：「國家立制，動必法天。

translations.literal: The first: restore the Department of State Affairs. It said, "When the state establishes institutions, it must always take heaven as its model.
translations.idiomatic: The first: restore the Department of State Affairs. It said, "When the state establishes institutions, it must always take heaven as its model.

sentences.zh: 尚書省上應玄象，對臨紫垣，故六卿擬喉舌之官，郎吏應星辰之位，斯實乾文昭著，故事具明。

translations.literal: The Department of State Affairs corresponds above to the dark asterism and faces the Purple Forbidden Enclosure; therefore the six ministers are set as the throat-and-tongue offices, and the bureau directors correspond to the positions of the stars—this truly makes the pattern of heaven manifest, and the precedent is fully clear.
translations.idiomatic: The Department of State Affairs corresponds above to the dark asterism and faces the Purple Forbidden Enclosure; therefore the six ministers stand as the throat-and-tongue offices, and the bureau directors match the stations of the stars. This truly manifests the pattern of heaven, and the precedent is fully clear.

sentences.zh: 方今省署，名實未稱。

translations.literal: At present the provincial offices in name and reality do not match.
translations.idiomatic: At present the provincial offices fall short of their names in practice.

sentences.zh: 夫三司使額，乃近代權制；

translations.literal: The title Commissioner of the Three Departments is a recent expedient of power;
translations.idiomatic: The title Commissioner of the Three Departments is a recent expedient of power;

sentences.zh: 判官、推官、勾院、開拆、磨勘、憑由、理欠、孔目、勾押、前後行，皆州郡吏局之名。

translations.literal: the posts of administrative aide, investigating aide, checking office, opening-and-sorting, audit, credentials, arrears settlement, clerks, checking clerk, front and rear runners—all are names from prefectural and district clerical offices.
translations.idiomatic: the posts of administrative aide, investigating aide, checking office, opening-and-sorting, audit, credentials, arrears settlement, clerks, checking clerk, and front and rear runners are all names drawn from prefectural and district clerical offices.

sentences.zh: 請廢三司，止於尚書省設六尚書分掌其事；

translations.literal: I beg that the Three Departments be abolished and only within the Department of State Affairs six ministers be set to divide their affairs;
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the Three Departments be abolished and that within the Department of State Affairs alone six ministers be established to divide their affairs;

sentences.zh: 廢判官、推官，設郎官分掌二十四司及左右司公事，使一人掌一司；

translations.literal: that administrative and investigating aides be abolished and bureau directors be set to divide the affairs of the twenty-four bureaus and the left and right secretariats, with one man in charge of each bureau;
translations.idiomatic: that administrative and investigating aides be abolished and bureau directors appointed to divide the affairs of the twenty-four bureaus and the left and right secretariats, with one man in charge of each bureau;

sentences.zh: 廢孔目、勾押、前後行為都事、主事、令史；

translations.literal: that clerks, checking clerks, and front and rear runners be abolished and replaced by chief clerks, clerks, and recorders;
translations.idiomatic: that clerks, checking clerks, and front and rear runners be abolished and replaced by chief clerks, clerks, and recorders;

sentences.zh: 廢勾院、開拆、磨勘、憑由、理欠等司歸比部及左右司。

translations.literal: that the checking office, opening-and-sorting, audit, credentials, arrears settlement, and other offices be abolished and returned to the Ministry of Comparisons and the left and right secretariats.
translations.idiomatic: that the checking office, opening-and-sorting, audit, credentials, arrears settlement, and other offices be abolished and returned to the Ministry of Comparisons and the left and right secretariats.

sentences.zh: 如此即事益精詳，且盡去州郡吏局之名也。

translations.literal: Thus affairs would be more precise in detail, and all names from prefectural and district clerical offices would be entirely removed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus affairs would be handled with greater precision, and all names borrowed from prefectural and district clerical offices would be entirely removed.

sentences.zh: 六卿如闕，即選名品相近、有才望者權之；

translations.literal: If a ministerial post is vacant, select a man of comparable standing and talent to act;
translations.idiomatic: If a ministerial post is vacant, select a man of comparable standing and talent to serve in an acting capacity;

sentences.zh: 郎官如闕，則於兩省三院選名幹有清望者，依資除之。

translations.literal: if a bureau director post is vacant, then from the two departments and three institutes choose a man of reputation and ability and appoint him according to seniority.
translations.idiomatic: if a bureau director post is vacant, choose from the two departments and three institutes a man of reputation and ability and appoint him according to seniority.

sentences.zh: 其二十四司公事，若繁簡不同，望下本省府屬參酌其類，均而行之。」

translations.literal: As for the affairs of the twenty-four bureaus, if their complexity differs, I beg that subordinates of this department be consulted to weigh their kinds and balance their execution."
translations.idiomatic: As for the affairs of the twenty-four bureaus, if their complexity differs, I beg that subordinates of this department be consulted to weigh their kinds and distribute the work evenly."

sentences.zh: 其二，慎公舉，曰：「朝廷頻年下詔，以類求人。

translations.literal: The second: be careful in public recommendation. It said, "In recent years the court has repeatedly issued edicts seeking men by category.
translations.idiomatic: The second: be careful in public recommendation. It said, "In recent years the court has repeatedly issued edicts seeking men by category.

sentences.zh: 但聞例得舉官，未見擇其舉主。

translations.literal: But one only hears of men obtaining office by quota of recommendation, and does not see selection of the recommender.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one hears only of men obtaining office through the quota of recommendation, and not of any scrutiny of the recommender.

sentences.zh: 欲望自今先責朝官有聲望者，各舉所知，其舉得官員則置籍，並舉主名姓籍之。

translations.literal: I desire that from now on court officials of reputation first be charged each to recommend those he knows; when the recommended obtain office, keep a register and also record the recommender's name.
translations.idiomatic: I desire that from now on court officials of established reputation first be charged each to recommend those he knows; when the recommended obtain office, keep a register and record the recommender's name as well.

sentences.zh: 所舉之官，實著廉能，則特旌舉主；

translations.literal: If the official recommended proves truly incorrupt and capable, then specially honor the recommender;
translations.idiomatic: If the official recommended proves truly incorrupt and capable, then specially honor the recommender;

sentences.zh: 若所舉貪冒敗事，連坐舉主。

translations.literal: if the one recommended is greedy and corrupt and ruins affairs, punish the recommender by association.
translations.idiomatic: if the one recommended proves greedy and corrupt and ruins affairs, punish the recommender by association.

sentences.zh: 陛下自登寶位，十年於茲，七經選掄，得人多矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, since ascending the throne, has been ten years at it; selection has been carried out seven times, and many men have been obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, since ascending the throne, has ruled for ten years; selection has been carried out seven times, and many able men have been obtained.

sentences.zh: 然下僚遠官，不無沉滯。

translations.literal: Yet among lower officials and distant magistrates there are still those sunk and stagnant.
translations.idiomatic: Yet among lower officials and distant magistrates some remain sunk in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 望令采訪司及州郡長吏，廉察以聞，籍以待用，則下無遺材矣。」

translations.literal: I beg that the Inspection Office and prefectural and district chief magistrates investigate and report, keep registers to await employment, and then there will be no talent left below."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the Inspection Office and prefectural and district chief magistrates investigate and report, keep registers to await employment, and then no talent below will be overlooked."

sentences.zh: 其三，懲貪吏，曰：「貪吏之於民，其損甚大。

translations.literal: The third: punish greedy officials. It said, "Greedy officials toward the people do very great harm.
translations.idiomatic: The third: punish greedy officials. It said, "Greedy officials do the people very great harm.

sentences.zh: 屈法煩刑，徇私肆虐，使民之受害甚於木之受蠹。

translations.literal: Bending law and heaping punishments, indulging private interest and raging tyrannically—the harm they do the people is worse than worms in wood.
translations.idiomatic: Bending the law and heaping punishments, indulging private interest and raging tyrannically—the harm they inflict on the people is worse than worms in timber.

sentences.zh: 若乃用非其人而不繩以法，雖夷、齊、顏、閔不能自見。

translations.literal: If one employs the wrong man and does not restrain him by law, even Yi, Qi, Yan, and Min could not make themselves seen.
translations.idiomatic: If one employs the wrong man and does not restrain him by law, even men like Boyi, Shuqi, Yan Hui, and Min Ziqian could not make their virtue visible.

sentences.zh: 蓋中人之性，如水之在器，方員不常，顧用之者何如爾。

translations.literal: For the nature of ordinary men is like water in a vessel—square or round is not fixed; it all depends on how one uses them.
translations.idiomatic: For the nature of ordinary men is like water in a vessel—square or round is not fixed; everything depends on how one employs them.

sentences.zh: 望令諸路轉運使副兼采訪之名，責以覺察州、府、軍、監長吏得失，俟其澄清部內，則待以不次之擢，置於侍從之間。

translations.literal: I beg that transport commissioners and their deputies be given the additional title of inspection, charged to detect the gains and losses of prefectural, district, army, and supervisory chief magistrates; when they have clarified their jurisdictions, then treat them to extraordinary promotion and place them among attendants.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that transport commissioners and their deputies be given the additional title of inspection and charged to detect the gains and losses of prefectural, district, army, and supervisory chief magistrates; when they have clarified their jurisdictions, reward them with extraordinary promotion and place them among the emperor's attendants.

sentences.zh: 所貴周知物理，能備顧問，且足為外官之勸也。」

translations.literal: This would be valuable for thorough knowledge of things and readiness as advisers, and would also suffice as encouragement to outer officials."
translations.idiomatic: This would be valuable for thorough knowledge of affairs and readiness as advisers, and would also serve as encouragement to officials in the provinces."

sentences.zh: 其四，省冗官，曰：「古人建官，初不必備者，惟得其人也。

translations.literal: The fourth: reduce superfluous officials. It said, "When the ancients established offices, at first they did not need to be fully staffed—only to obtain the right men.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth: reduce superfluous officials. It said, "When the ancients established offices, they did not at first need to fill every post—only to obtain the right men.

sentences.zh: 國家封疆雖逾前世，而分設庶官實倍常數，意欲盡籠天下之利，而民物轉加凋弊。

translations.literal: Our state's territory exceeds past dynasties, yet the various offices set out are truly double the usual number; the intent is to gather all profit under heaven, yet the people's goods grow ever more exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Our state's territory exceeds that of past dynasties, yet the various offices established are truly double the usual number; the intent is to gather all profit under heaven, yet the people's goods grow ever more exhausted.

sentences.zh: 二十年前，江、淮諸郡，揚、楚最居要衝，務穰事眾，地廣民繁。

translations.literal: Twenty years ago, among the prefectures along the Yangzi and Huai, Yang and Chu were most strategically vital, with heavy harvest duties and many affairs, broad territory and a dense population.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years ago, among the prefectures along the Yangzi and Huai, Yang and Chu were the most strategically vital, with heavy harvest duties and many affairs, broad territory and a dense population.

sentences.zh: 然止設知州一人署領官事，其餘通判官、推官及州官等，悉皆分管榷務、倉庫。

translations.literal: Yet only one prefect was set to oversee official affairs; the rest—deputy prefect, investigating aide, and prefectural officials—all divided management of monopoly duties and storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: Yet only one prefect was appointed to oversee official affairs; the rest—the deputy prefect, investigating aide, and prefectural officials—all divided management of monopoly duties and storehouses.

sentences.zh: 當時事無不集，兼少獄訟。

translations.literal: At that time nothing failed to be gathered, and lawsuits were also few.
translations.idiomatic: At that time nothing failed to be accomplished, and lawsuits were few as well.

sentences.zh: 其後十年，臣任揚州時，朝廷添置監臨、使臣等職，實逾本州官數。

translations.literal: Ten years later, when I served at Yangzhou, the court added supervisory and envoy posts, which truly exceeded the original number of this prefecture's officials.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later, when I served at Yangzhou, the court added supervisory and envoy posts that truly exceeded the original number of officials in that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 諸州冗員，似此非一。

translations.literal: Superfluous posts in the prefectures are like this and not only one.
translations.idiomatic: Superfluous posts in the prefectures are like this in more than one place.

sentences.zh: 今以朝官、諸色使臣及縣令、簿、尉等高卑相折而計之，一人月費不啻十千，以千人約之，歲計用十餘萬千，更倍萬約之，萬又過倍。

translations.literal: Now counting court officials, envoys of various ranks, and magistrates, registrars, and constables high and low against one another, one man's monthly cost is no less than ten thousand cash; estimating for a thousand men, yearly use is more than a hundred million; doubling the ten thousands again, ten thousand passes double again.
translations.idiomatic: Now, counting court officials, envoys of various ranks, and magistrates, registrars, and constables high and low together, one man's monthly cost is no less than ten thousand cash; estimating for a thousand men, yearly expenditure runs to more than a hundred million; double that figure again, and ten thousand becomes more than double once more.

sentences.zh: 使皆廉吏，止糜公帑；

translations.literal: If all were honest officials, they would only waste the public treasury;
translations.idiomatic: If all were honest officials, they would only drain the public treasury;

sentences.zh: 設或貪夫參錯其間，則取於民者又加倍焉。

translations.literal: but suppose greedy men are mixed among them, then what is taken from the people is doubled again.
translations.idiomatic: but if greedy men are mixed among them, what is taken from the people is doubled again.

sentences.zh: 望委各路轉運使副，與知州同議裁減。

translations.literal: I beg that transport commissioners and deputies discuss reduction jointly with prefects.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that transport commissioners and deputies discuss reductions jointly with prefects.

sentences.zh: 若縣令、簿、尉等官自前多不備置，可兼者兼之，如此則冗官汰矣。」

translations.literal: If magistrates, registrars, constables, and such posts were formerly often not fully staffed, where posts can be combined let them be combined; thus superfluous officials would be eliminated."
translations.idiomatic: Where magistrates, registrars, constables, and such posts were formerly often not fully staffed, let combined posts be combined where possible; thus superfluous officials would be eliminated."

sentences.zh: 其五，擇遠官，曰：「負罪之人，多非良善，貪殘凶暴，無所不至。

translations.literal: The fifth: select distant officials. It said, "Men bearing guilt are mostly not good; greedy, cruel, and violent, there is nothing they will not do.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth: select distant officials. It said, "Men bearing guilt are mostly not good; greedy, cruel, and violent, there is nothing they will not do.

sentences.zh: 若授以遠方牧民之官，其或怙惡不悛，恃遠肆毒。

translations.literal: If given distant posts as shepherds of the people, some may cling to evil and not reform, relying on distance to unleash poison.
translations.idiomatic: If given distant posts as shepherds of the people, some may cling to evil and refuse to reform, relying on distance to unleash their poison.

sentences.zh: 小民罹殃，卒莫上訴，甚非撫綏遠人之意也。

translations.literal: The common people suffer disaster and in the end cannot appeal above—this is very far from the intent to soothe distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: The common people suffer disaster and in the end cannot appeal above—this falls very far short of the intent to soothe distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 若自今以往，西川、廣南長吏不任負罪之人，則遠人受賜矣。」

translations.literal: If from now on chief magistrates of Xichuan and Guangnan are not assigned men bearing guilt, then distant peoples will receive the gift."
translations.idiomatic: If from now on chief magistrates of Xichuan and Guangnan are not assigned men bearing guilt, then distant peoples will receive a true benefit."

sentences.zh: 書奏，太宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Taizong emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the Taizong emperor praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 初，柴禹錫任樞密，有奴受人金，而禹錫實不知也。

translations.literal: Previously, when Chai Yuxi held the Bureau of Military Affairs, a slave accepted gold from someone, yet Yuxi truly did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when Chai Yuxi held the Bureau of Military Affairs, a slave accepted gold from someone, though Yuxi truly did not know of it.

sentences.zh: 參知政事陳恕欲因以中禹錫。

translations.literal: Associate Administrator Chen Shu wished to use this to strike at Yuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Associate Administrator Chen Shu wished to use this to strike at Yuxi.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒，引囚訊其事，化基為辨其誣。

translations.literal: The Taizong emperor was angry and summoned the prisoner to question the matter; Huaji argued that it was a false charge.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong emperor was angry and summoned the prisoner to question the matter; Huaji argued that the charge was false.

sentences.zh: 太宗感悟，以化基為長者。

translations.literal: The Taizong emperor came to his senses and regarded Huaji as a man of mature judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong emperor came to his senses and regarded Huaji as a man of mature judgment.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，拜中丞，俄知京朝官考課，遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: During Chunhua he was appointed Censor-in-Chief, and soon after made director of capital official performance review, then transferred to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunhua he was appointed Censor-in-Chief, and soon after made director of capital official performance review, then transferred to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 至道三年，超拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhidao he was abruptly promoted to Associate Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhidao he was abruptly promoted to Associate Administrator.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年，以工部尚書罷知揚州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping he was dismissed as Minister of Works and made prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianping he left the central administration as Minister of Works and was made prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 移知河南府，進禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Henan and advanced to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Henan and advanced to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年，卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died, aged sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈右僕射，諡惠獻。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the post of Right Vice Director and the posthumous title Huixian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the post of Right Vice Director and the posthumous title Huixian.

sentences.zh: 化基寬厚有容，喜慍不形，僚佐有相淩慢者，輒優容之。

translations.literal: Huaji was generous and forbearing, showing neither joy nor anger; when subordinates were somewhat disrespectful, he always treated them with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji was generous and forbearing, never showing joy or anger on his face; when subordinates were somewhat disrespectful, he always treated them with indulgence.

sentences.zh: 在中書，不以蔭補諸子官，然善教訓，故其子舉正、舉直、舉善、舉元皆有所立。

translations.literal: While at the Central Secretariat he did not use yin privilege to secure offices for his sons, yet he taught them well; therefore his sons Juzheng, Juzhi, Jushan, and Juyuan each achieved distinction.
translations.idiomatic: While serving at the Central Secretariat he would not use yin privilege to place his sons in office, yet he trained them well; as a result his sons Juzheng, Juzhi, Jushan, and Juyuan each made names for themselves.

sentences.zh: 子 舉正

translations.literal: Son: Juzheng
translations.idiomatic: Son: Juzheng

sentences.zh: 舉正，字伯仲，幼嗜學，厚重寡言。

translations.literal: Juzheng, styled Bozhong, from childhood loved learning; he was grave, substantial, and sparing of speech.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng, courtesy name Bozhong, loved learning from childhood; he was grave and substantial, and spoke little.

sentences.zh: 化基以為類己，器愛異諸子，以蔭補秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Huaji regarded him as like himself, valued and loved him above the other sons, and had him appointed by yin privilege as collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji saw in him a temperament like his own, cherished him above his other sons, and secured for him a yin-privilege appointment as collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，知伊闕、任丘縣，館閣校勘、集賢校理、《真宗實錄》院檢討、國史編修官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, served as magistrate of Yique and Renqiu counties, and held posts as Hanlin collation editor, collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, reviewer in the Veritable Records of Zhenzong office, and compiler of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and governed Yique and Renqiu counties, then served as a Hanlin collation editor, collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, reviewer for the Veritable Records of Zhenzong, and compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 三遷尚書度支員外郎、直集賢院，修《三朝寶訓》，同修起居注，擢知制誥。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Vice Director of Revenue in the Ministry of Revenue and direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, helped compile the Precious Instructions of Three Reigns, jointly compiled the Diary of Actions and Repose, and was promoted to drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted three times, he became Vice Director of Revenue in the Ministry of Revenue and a direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, helped compile the Precious Instructions of Three Reigns, served as co-compiler of the Diary of Actions and Repose, and was elevated to drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 其妻父陳堯佐為相，改龍圖閣待制、堯佐罷，以兵部郎中復知制誥，為翰林學士，拜右諫議大夫、參知政事。

translations.literal: When his father-in-law Chen Yaozuo became chief councilor, he was changed to attendant of the Dragon Diagram Hall; after Yaozuo was dismissed he was again made drafter of edicts as Director in the Ministry of War, became Hanlin academician, and was appointed Right Remonstrator and Participant in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: When his father-in-law Chen Yaozuo became chief councilor, he was reassigned as attendant of the Dragon Diagram Hall; after Yaozuo left office he returned to drafting edicts as Director in the Ministry of War, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed Right Remonstrator and Participant in Governance.

sentences.zh: 前一日，吏有馳報者，舉正方燕居齋舍，徐謂吏曰：「安得漏禁中語？」

translations.literal: The day before, when a clerk came galloping with the news, Juzheng was at leisure in his study quarters and said calmly to the clerk, "How could palace talk be leaked?"
translations.idiomatic: The day before, when a clerk came galloping with the news, Juzheng was at leisure in his study and said calmly to the clerk, "How could talk from within the palace have been leaked?"

sentences.zh: 既入謝，仁宗曰：「卿恬於進取，未嘗干朝廷以私，故不次用卿。」

translations.literal: When he entered to give thanks, Renzong said, "You are indifferent to advancement and have never importuned the court for private ends; therefore We have appointed you out of turn."
translations.idiomatic: When he came in to give thanks, Emperor Renzong said, "You are indifferent to advancement and have never importuned the court for private ends; that is why We have promoted you out of turn."

sentences.zh: 時陝西用兵，呂夷簡以宰相判樞密院，舉正曰：「判名重，不可不避也。」

translations.literal: At the time war was being waged in Shaanxi; Lü Yijian as chief councilor concurrently directed the Bureau of Military Affairs. Juzheng said, "The title of concurrent director is weighty and cannot be accepted without avoidance."
translations.idiomatic: War was then being waged in Shaanxi, and Lü Yijian as chief councilor was concurrently directing the Bureau of Military Affairs. Juzheng said, "The title of concurrent director carries great weight and ought not to be accepted without stepping aside."

sentences.zh: 乃改兼樞密使。

translations.literal: He was therefore changed to concurrent Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore reassigned as concurrent Military Affairs Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Impartial in Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Impartial in Affairs.

sentences.zh: 御史臺舉李徽之為御史，舉正友婿也，格不行。

translations.literal: The Censorate nominated Li Huizhi as censor; he was the friend and son-in-law of Juzheng, and the nomination was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate nominated Li Huizhi for censor, but as he was Juzheng's friend and son-in-law the nomination was blocked.

sentences.zh: 徽之訟曰：「舉正妻悍不能制，如謀國何？」

translations.literal: Huizhi sued, saying, "Juzheng's wife is fierce and he cannot control her—how can he plan for the state?"
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi brought suit, saying, "Juzheng's wife is fierce and he cannot control her—how can such a man plan for the state?"

sentences.zh: 歐陽修等亦論舉正懦默不任事，舉正亦自求去，遂以資政殿學士、尚書禮部侍郎知許州。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu and others also criticized Juzheng as timid, silent, and unfit for office; Juzheng also asked to resign, and was made Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance, Vice Minister of Rites in the Ministry of Rites, and prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu and others also argued that Juzheng was timid, silent, and unfit for office. Juzheng asked to resign as well and was made Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance, Vice Minister of Rites, and prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 光化軍叛卒轉寇傍境，而州兵有謀起為應者，舉正潛捕首惡者斬之。

translations.literal: Mutinous soldiers of Guanghua Army turned to raid neighboring districts, and local troops plotted to rise in response; Juzheng secretly seized the ringleaders and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Mutinous soldiers of Guanghua Army turned to raid neighboring districts, and some local troops plotted to rise in support; Juzheng secretly seized the ringleaders and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 徙知應天府，累遷左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Yingtianfu and was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Yingtianfu and rose in stages to Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 皇佑初，拜御史中丞，乃奏：「張堯佐庸人，緣妃家，一日領四使，使賢士大夫無所勸。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangyou he was appointed Censor-in-Chief and memorialized, "Zhang Yaozuo is a mediocrity who rose through the imperial consort's family; in a single day he received four commissioner posts, leaving worthy scholar-officials with nothing to strive for."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangyou he was made Censor-in-Chief and memorialized, "Zhang Yaozuo is a mediocrity who rose through the imperial consort's family. In a single day he received four commissioner posts, leaving worthy scholar-officials nothing to strive for."

sentences.zh: 不報，舉正因留班廷諍，乃奪宣徽、景靈二使。

translations.literal: There was no response; Juzheng therefore remained after court to remonstrate in the hall, and the two posts of Xuanhui and Jingling commissioners were taken away.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not respond. Juzheng therefore remained after audience to remonstrate in the hall, and the Xuanhui and Jingling commissioner posts were stripped away.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「先朝用人，雖守邊累年者，官止遙郡刺史。

translations.literal: He also said, "In the previous reign appointments were made so that even those who guarded the frontier for many years reached only remote prefectural governor.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Under the previous reign, even men who guarded the frontier for many years rose no higher than remote prefectural governor.

sentences.zh: 今所用未盡得人，而克期待遷，使後有功者何所勸耶？

translations.literal: Those appointed now are not all the right men, yet they expect swift promotion—what will encourage those who achieve merit later?
translations.idiomatic: Those appointed now are not all the right men, yet they still expect swift promotion. What will encourage those who earn merit later?

sentences.zh: 且轉運使察官吏能否，生民休戚賴焉。

translations.literal: Moreover, transport commissioners inspect whether officials are capable; the people's weal and woe depend on them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, transport commissioners judge whether officials are capable, and the people's welfare depends on them.

sentences.zh: 命甫下而數更，不終歲而再易，恩澤所以未宣，民疾所以未瘳者，職此故也。」

translations.literal: Orders have just been issued and are changed several times; within a year they are replaced again—this is why imperial grace is not spread abroad and why the people's afflictions are not healed."
translations.idiomatic: Orders are barely issued before they are changed again, and appointments rarely last a year. That is why imperial grace does not reach the people and why their afflictions are not healed."

sentences.zh: 御史唐介坐言事貶春州，舉正力言之，介得徙英州。

translations.literal: Censor Tang Jie was demoted to Chunzhou for speaking out on affairs; Juzheng argued forcefully on his behalf, and Jie was transferred to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Tang Jie was demoted to Chunzhou for speaking out on state affairs. Juzheng argued forcefully on his behalf, and Jie was transferred to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 居半歲，堯佐復為宣徽使，家居凡七上疏。

translations.literal: After half a year Yaozuo was again made Xuanhui commissioner; while at home Juzheng submitted seven memorials in all.
translations.idiomatic: Half a year later Yaozuo was again made Xuanhui commissioner. While at home Juzheng submitted seven memorials in all.

sentences.zh: 及狄青為樞密使，又言青出兵伍不可為執政，力爭不能奪，因請解言職。

translations.literal: When Di Qing became Military Affairs Commissioner, he again said Qing had risen from the ranks and could not serve in high governance; he argued strenuously but could not prevail, and therefore asked to be relieved of his remonstrance duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Di Qing became Military Affairs Commissioner, he again argued that a man raised from the ranks could not hold high governance. He fought the appointment strenuously but could not prevail, and therefore asked to be relieved of his remonstrance duties.

sentences.zh: 帝稱其得風憲體，遣賜就第，賜白金三百兩，除觀文殿學士、禮部尚書、知河南府，入兼翰林侍讀學士。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him for grasping the censorial spirit, sent gifts to his residence, bestowed three hundred taels of white silver, appointed him Academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture, Minister of Rites, and prefect of Henan, and had him enter as concurrent Hanlin attendant reader.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him for grasping the censorial spirit, sent gifts to his home, bestowed three hundred taels of white silver, appointed him Academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture, Minister of Rites, and prefect of Henan, and made him a concurrent Hanlin attendant reader.

sentences.zh: 每進讀及前代治亂之際，必再三諷諭。

translations.literal: Whenever he lectured before the throne and reached passages on order and disorder in former ages, he would admonish again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he lectured before the throne and reached passages on order and disorder in former ages, he would admonish the emperor again and again.

sentences.zh: 以太子少傅致仕，卒，贈太子太保，諡安簡，賜黃金百兩。

translations.literal: He retired as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, died, was posthumously given Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, posthumous title Anjian, and a gift of one hundred taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and died. He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the posthumous title Anjian, and granted one hundred taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 文章雅厚如其為人，有《平山集》、《中書制集》、《內制集》五十卷。

translations.literal: His writings were elegant and substantial like the man himself; he left the Pingshan Collection, Central Secretariat Draft Collection, and Inner Draft Collection in fifty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His writings were as elegant and substantial as the man himself. He left the Pingshan Collection, Central Secretariat Draft Collection, and Inner Draft Collection in fifty juan.

sentences.zh: 子 舉元

translations.literal: Son: Juyuan
translations.idiomatic: Son: Juyuan

sentences.zh: 舉元，字懿臣，以上文章賜進士出身。

translations.literal: Juyuan, styled Yichen, was granted jinshi standing by imperial favor for superior literary compositions.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan, courtesy name Yichen, was granted jinshi standing by imperial favor for his superior literary compositions.

sentences.zh: 知潮州，江水敗堤，盜乘間竊發，舉元夜召里豪計事，盜既獲，乃治堤。

translations.literal: As prefect of Chaozhou, when river water breached the dikes bandits seized the moment to rise; Juyuan summoned local leaders by night to plan, and once the bandits were captured he repaired the dikes.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Chaozhou, when floodwaters breached the dikes bandits seized the moment to rise. Juyuan summoned local leaders by night to plan the response; once the bandits were captured, he repaired the dikes.

sentences.zh: 為河陰發運判官，或言大河決，將犯京師，舉元適入對，具論地形證其妄，已而果然。

translations.literal: As transport judge of Heyin, when someone said the Great River had burst and would threaten the capital, Juyuan happened to attend audience and fully argued from terrain that this was false—and so it proved.
translations.idiomatic: As transport judge of Heyin, when reports said the Yellow River had burst and would threaten the capital, Juyuan happened to attend audience and argued from the terrain that the alarm was false—and so it proved.

sentences.zh: 歷郡牧、戶部判官、京東轉運使。

translations.literal: He successively served as prefect, judge in the Ministry of Revenue, and transport commissioner of Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect, judge in the Ministry of Revenue, and transport commissioner of Jingdong.

sentences.zh: 沙門島多流人，守吏顧貨橐，陰殺之。

translations.literal: Shamen Island held many exiles; guarding officials eyed their goods and secretly killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Shamen Island held many exiles, and the guarding officials eyed their goods and secretly killed them.

sentences.zh: 舉元請立監以較賞罰，自是全活者眾。

translations.literal: Juyuan requested establishment of a supervisory office to weigh rewards and punishments; from then on many more were kept alive.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan asked that a supervisory office be established to weigh rewards and punishments, and from then on far more exiles were kept alive.

sentences.zh: 徙淮南、河東。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Huainan and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Huainan and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 夏人來爭屈野地，舉元從數騎度河，設幕與之議，示以赤心，夏人感服。

translations.literal: When the Xia came to dispute Quye territory, Juyuan crossed the river with a few horsemen, pitched a tent to negotiate with them, and showed his sincere heart; the Xia were moved and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia came to dispute Quye territory, Juyuan crossed the river with only a few horsemen, pitched a tent to negotiate with them, and showed his sincere heart. The Xia were moved and submitted.

sentences.zh: 治平中，又徙成都。

translations.literal: During the Zhiping era he was again transferred to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiping era he was transferred again to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 邙井鹽歲入二百五十萬，為丹棱卓箇所侵，積不售，下令止之，鹽登於舊。

translations.literal: Mangjing salt yielded 2,500,000 in annual revenue but was encroached upon by Danling Zhuoge; stocks piled up unsold. He ordered this stopped, and salt revenues returned to their former level.
translations.idiomatic: Mangjing salt yielded 2,500,000 in annual revenue but was being encroached upon by Danling Zhuoge, leaving stocks piled up unsold. He ordered the encroachment stopped, and salt revenues returned to their former level.

sentences.zh: 召提舉在京修造，英宗勞之曰：「官廬舍害於水，僅有存者，卿究心公家，毋憚其勞。」

translations.literal: He was summoned to supervise capital repairs. Emperor Yingzong encouraged him, saying, "Official residences have suffered from water; only a few remain. Devote yourself to the public service and do not shrink from the labor."
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to supervise capital repairs. Emperor Yingzong encouraged him, saying, "Official residences have suffered from flood; only a few remain. Devote yourself wholeheartedly to the public service and do not shrink from the labor."

sentences.zh: 俄進鹽鐵副使，拜天章閣待制，知滄州，改河北都轉運使，知永興軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted Vice Commissioner of Salt and Iron, appointed attendant of the Heavenly Writings Hall, made prefect of Cangzhou, changed to overall transport commissioner of Hebei, and made military commissioner of Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted Vice Commissioner of Salt and Iron, made attendant of the Heavenly Writings Hall and prefect of Cangzhou, then overall transport commissioner of Hebei and military commissioner of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 慶人、夏人屯境上，有窺我意，舉元使二裨將以千騎扼其要害。

translations.literal: Qing people and Xia people camped on the border, seeming to probe our intentions; Juyuan sent two lieutenant generals with a thousand horsemen to hold their vital points.
translations.idiomatic: Qing and Xia forces camped on the border as if to probe our intentions. Juyuan sent two lieutenant generals with a thousand horsemen to hold the vital passes.

sentences.zh: 長安遣從事來會兵涇原，戒勿輕舉。

translations.literal: Chang'an sent an aide to join forces at Jingyuan and warned against rash action.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an sent an aide to join forces at Jingyuan and warned against rash action.

sentences.zh: 大將竇舜卿銳意請行，不聽。

translations.literal: The great general Dou Shunqing eagerly asked to go forth, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The great general Dou Shunqing eagerly asked to take the field, but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 舉元曰：「不過三日，虜去矣。」

translations.literal: Juyuan said, "Within three days at most the barbarians will withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan said, "Within three days at most the enemy will withdraw."

sentences.zh: 至期果去。

translations.literal: When the day came they indeed withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came they indeed withdrew.

sentences.zh: 神宗以細劄諮攻守策，舉元請省官減戍，益備去兵，勿營亭障。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong consulted him by detailed note on offensive and defensive strategy; Juyuan asked to reduce officials and border garrisons, increase preparedness while withdrawing forward troops, and not build pavilions and stockade barriers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong consulted him by detailed note on offensive and defensive strategy. Juyuan recommended reducing officials and border garrisons, increasing preparedness while withdrawing forward troops, and not building pavilions and stockade barriers.

sentences.zh: 輿論不合，遂引疾求解，徙陳州，未行而卒。

translations.literal: Public opinion did not agree; he therefore cited illness and asked to resign, was transferred to Chenzhou, and died before he could depart.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion did not agree. He therefore cited illness and asked to resign, was transferred to Chenzhou, and died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 官至給事中，年六十二。

translations.literal: He reached the office of Impartial in Affairs and died at sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Impartial in Affairs and died at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 子詔。

translations.literal: His son was Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhao.

sentences.zh: 孫 詔

translations.literal: Grandson: Zhao
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Zhao

sentences.zh: 詔，字景獻，用蔭補官，通判廣信軍事，知博州。

translations.literal: Zhao, styled Jingxian, entered office by yin privilege, served as military vice prefect of Guangxin, and was prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, courtesy name Jingxian, entered office by yin privilege, served as military vice prefect of Guangxin, and governed Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 魏俗尚椎剽，姦盜相囊橐，詔請開反告殺並贖罪法，以攜其黨。

translations.literal: Wei custom favored violent robbery; villains and thieves backed one another. Zhao asked to revive the law of counter-accusation leading to execution with commutation through fines, to break up their factions.
translations.idiomatic: Wei custom favored violent robbery, and villains and thieves backed one another. Zhao asked to revive the law allowing counter-accusation to execution with commutation through fines, so as to break up their factions.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，朝廷起回河之議，未決，而開河之役遽興。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou the court raised debate on redirecting the river; before a decision was reached, work to open the channel was suddenly launched.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanyou the court raised debate on redirecting the river. Before a decision was reached, work to open the channel was suddenly launched.

sentences.zh: 詔言：「河朔秋潦，水淫為災，民人流徙，賴發廩振贍恩，稍蘇其生，謂宜安之，未可以力役傷也。」

translations.literal: Zhao said, "In autumn the Hebei region suffered floods; excessive water brought disaster and the people were displaced. They have barely revived through granary relief and sustaining grace. They ought to be settled in peace and must not be harmed by forced labor."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "In autumn the Hebei region suffered floods. Excessive water brought disaster and the people were displaced. They have barely revived through granary relief and sustaining grace. They ought to be settled in peace and must not be harmed by forced labor."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The court followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 擢開封府推官。

translations.literal: He was promoted investigating officer of Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted investigating officer of Kaifeng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 富民貸後絕僧牒為緡錢三十萬，逾期復責倍輸，身死貲籍，又錮其妻子，詔請免之。

translations.literal: A wealthy man had borrowed money and later had his monk certificate invalidated for a debt of three hundred thousand strings of cash; when overdue he was charged double payment, died with his estate seized, and his wife and children were imprisoned—Zhao asked that they be released.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy man had borrowed money and later had his monk certificate invalidated for a debt of three hundred thousand strings of cash. When he fell overdue he was charged double payment, died with his estate seized, and his wife and children were imprisoned. Zhao asked that they be released.

sentences.zh: 出為滑州，州屬縣有退灘百餘頃，歲調民刈草給河堤，民病其役，詔募人佃之，而收其餘。

translations.literal: Sent out as prefect of Huazhou, a subordinate county had more than a hundred qing of receded shoals; each year the people were levied to cut grass for the river dikes and suffered under the labor. Zhao had the land leased out and took the surplus revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as prefect of Huazhou, he found that a subordinate county had more than a hundred qing of receded shoals. Each year the people were levied to cut grass for the river dikes and suffered under the labor. Zhao had the land leased out and took the surplus revenue.

sentences.zh: 為度支郎中，使契丹，時方討西夏，迓者耶律誠欲嘗我，言曰：「河西無禮，大國能容之乎？」

translations.literal: As Director in the Revenue Section he was envoy to Khitan; at the time the court was campaigning against Western Xia. The welcoming officer Yelü Cheng wished to test us and said, "The Hexi people are without propriety—can the great state tolerate them?"
translations.idiomatic: As Director in the Revenue Section he served as envoy to Khitan while the court was campaigning against Western Xia. The welcoming officer Yelü Cheng wished to test the Song and said, "The Hexi people are without propriety—can the great state tolerate them?"

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「夏人侮邊，既正其罪矣，何預兩朝和好事？」

translations.literal: Zhao said, "The Xia have insulted the border and their offense has already been corrected—what has that to do with the good relations of our two courts?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "The Xia have insulted the border and their offense has already been corrected. What has that to do with the good relations of our two courts?"

sentences.zh: 入賀，故事，跪而飲，蓋有誤拜者，乃強詔，詔曰：「南北百年，所守者禮，其可紛更耶？」

translations.literal: When he entered to offer congratulations, by precedent one knelt to drink; there had been those who bowed incorrectly, so they tried to force Zhao. Zhao said, "North and South have stood for a hundred years; what we observe is ritual—how can it be changed recklessly?"
translations.idiomatic: When he entered to offer congratulations, by precedent one knelt to drink. Because some had bowed incorrectly, they tried to force Zhao. Zhao said, "North and South have stood for a hundred years. What we observe is ritual—how can it be changed recklessly?"

sentences.zh: 卒跪飲之。

translations.literal: In the end he knelt and drank.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he knelt and drank.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中，由大理少卿為卿，徙司農。

translations.literal: During Chongning he rose from Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review to Director, then was transferred to Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: During Chongning he rose from Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review to Director, then was transferred to Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 御史論詔在滁日請蘇軾書《醉翁亭碑》，罷主崇福宮。

translations.literal: Censors charged that while in Chuzhou Zhao had asked Su Shi to write the Stele of the Drunken Old Man Pavilion; he was dismissed and made custodian of Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Censors charged that while in Chuzhou Zhao had asked Su Shi to write the Stele of the Drunken Old Man Pavilion. He was dismissed and made custodian of Chongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 旋知汝州，鑄錢卒罵大校，詔斬以徇，而上章待罪。

translations.literal: Soon he was made prefect of Ruzhou; coin-casting soldiers cursed a senior officer, and Zhao had them executed as a warning, then submitted a memorial awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made prefect of Ruzhou. Coin-casting soldiers cursed a senior officer, and Zhao had them executed as a warning, then submitted a memorial awaiting punishment.

sentences.zh: 除直秘閣，言者復抉滁州事，罷去。

translations.literal: He was appointed direct academician of the Secret Archive, but critics again dredged up the Chuzhou affair and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed direct academician of the Secret Archive, but critics again dredged up the Chuzhou affair and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 起知深、兗二州，徙同州，過闕，留為左司郎中，遷衛尉、太府卿、刑部侍郎，詳定敕令。

translations.literal: He was recalled to govern Shen and Yan prefectures, transferred to Tongzhou, passed through the capital and was retained as Left Department Director, then promoted Commandant of the Guard, Minister of the Palace Storehouse, Vice Minister of Punishments, and charged with revising statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to govern Shen and Yan prefectures, transferred to Tongzhou, passed through the capital and was retained as Left Department Director, then promoted Commandant of the Guard, Minister of the Palace Storehouse, Vice Minister of Punishments, and charged with revising statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 舊借緋紫者不佩魚，詔言：「章服所以辨上下，今與胥吏不異。」

translations.literal: Formerly those who borrowed scarlet and purple did not wear fish pendants. Zhao said, "Court dress distinguishes high and low; now they are no different from clerks."
translations.idiomatic: Formerly those who borrowed scarlet and purple robes did not wear fish pendants. Zhao said, "Court dress distinguishes high from low, yet now they are no different from clerks."

sentences.zh: 遂皆佩魚。

translations.literal: They were therefore all made to wear fish pendants.
translations.idiomatic: They were therefore all required to wear fish pendants.

sentences.zh: 歷工、兵、戶三部侍郎，轉開封尹。

translations.literal: He passed through the vice ministries of Works, War, and Revenue, then became Prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice minister of Works, War, and Revenue in turn, then became Prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 時子璹使京西，攝尹洛。

translations.literal: At the time his son Jun was envoy to Jingxi and acted as prefect of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his son Jun was envoy to Jingxi and acted as prefect of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 父子兩京相望，人以為榮。

translations.literal: Father and son faced each other across the two capitals, and people regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son faced each other across the two capitals, and people regarded it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 進刑部尚書，拜延康殿學士，提舉上清寶籙宮，復為工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Minister of Punishments, appointed Academician of the Yankang Hall, made custodian of the Shangqing Precious Registers Palace, and again made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Minister of Punishments, appointed Academician of the Yankang Hall, made custodian of the Shangqing Precious Registers Palace, and again made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 徽宗閔其老，命毋拜，詔惶恐，於是但朝朔望。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong pitied his age and ordered that he need not bow; Zhao was fearful and thereafter attended court only on the first and fifteenth.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong pitied his age and ordered that he need not bow. Zhao was fearful and thereafter attended court only on the first and fifteenth of the month.

sentences.zh: 俄以銀青光祿大夫致仕，卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: Soon he retired as Silver-Gleaming Grandee for Splendid Happiness, died, and was seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he retired as Silver-Gleaming Grandee for Splendid Happiness and died at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自昔參大政、贊機務，非明敏特達之士，不能勝其任。

translations.literal: The critique says: From antiquity, to participate in great governance and assist in state affairs, unless one is bright, keen, and outstanding, one cannot bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: The critique says: From antiquity, to participate in great governance and assist in state affairs, only a man who is bright, keen, and outstanding can bear the burden.

sentences.zh: 若又飭以文雅，濟以治具，則盡善矣。

translations.literal: If in addition he is disciplined by refinement and supplied with the tools of governance, then he is complete.
translations.idiomatic: If in addition he is disciplined by refinement and supplied with the tools of governance, then he is complete.

sentences.zh: 若水機鑒明敏，儒而知兵；

translations.literal: Ruoshui was keen in insight and bright; a scholar who understood warfare;
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui was keen in insight and bright, a scholar who understood warfare;

sentences.zh: 李至剛嚴簡重，好古博雅，其於柄用宜矣。

translations.literal: Li Zhi was firm, stern, simple, and weighty, fond of antiquity and broad in learning—fit indeed to wield power.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi was firm, stern, simple, and weighty, fond of antiquity and broad in learning—fit indeed to wield power.

sentences.zh: 王沔臨事精密，能遠私謁，而考課之議，頗傷苛刻；

translations.literal: Wang Mian was precise in handling affairs and could keep private petitions at a distance, yet his proposals on performance review were rather harsh;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mian was precise in handling affairs and could keep private petitions at a distance, yet his proposals on performance review were rather harsh;

sentences.zh: 仲甫以吏事為時用，未免苟容之誚，瑕瑜固不相掩也。

translations.literal: Zhongfu was valued by the age for administrative skill, yet could not escape criticism for easy indulgence; flaw and merit indeed do not conceal one another.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu was valued by the age for administrative skill, yet could not escape criticism for easy indulgence; flaw and merit indeed do not conceal one another.

sentences.zh: 仲舒見舉於蒙正，而反攻其短；

translations.literal: Zhongshu was promoted by Mengzheng yet turned to attack his faults;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu was promoted by Mengzheng yet turned to attack his faults;

sentences.zh: 易簡不能周恤光逢，而置之死地，其不可與郭贄辨曹彬之誣、化基伸禹錫之枉同日而語也明矣。

translations.literal: Yijian could not show comprehensive care for Guangfeng and put him to death—it is clear this cannot be spoken of in the same day as Guo Zhi's refuting Cao Bin's false charge or Huaji's righting Chai Yuxi's wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian could not show comprehensive care for Guangfeng and put him to death. Clearly this cannot be spoken of in the same breath as Guo Zhi's refuting Cao Bin's false charge or Huaji's righting Chai Yuxi's wrong.

sentences.zh: 此純厚長者之稱，所以獨歸於二子歟！

translations.literal: This reputation for pure generosity and senior virtue—is it not for those two alone!
translations.idiomatic: This reputation for pure generosity and senior virtue belongs to those two alone!

sentences.zh: 舉正繼踐臺佐，得風憲體；

translations.literal: Juzheng followed in censorial service and grasped the censorial spirit;
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng followed in censorial service and grasped the censorial spirit;

sentences.zh: 舉元任職邊郡，有持重稱。

translations.literal: Juyuan served on the frontier and had a reputation for steadiness.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan served on the frontier and had a reputation for steadiness.

sentences.zh: 矧詔之父子又並尹兩京，克濟其美，何王氏子孫之多賢也！

translations.literal: Moreover, Zhao and his son together governed the two capitals, fulfilling their excellence—how many worthy men among the Wang clan's descendants!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Zhao and his son together governed the two capitals, fulfilling their excellence. How many worthy men there are among the Wang clan's descendants!
